COMBAT SYSTEMS

Damage

How attack power, defense, fatigue, and Poison affect HP loss.

Damage is the HP a character loses from an attack. The game starts with the attacker’s power, subtracts the defender’s defense, then applies Luck, elemental resistance, and random variation.

The damage formula

Physical attacks and damaging magic share this ordinary calculation. Click any linked term to see what it means.

ORDINARY SUCCESSFUL ATTACK
Damage = (Attack power − Defense + Luck difference) × (100 − Elemental resistance) 100 × Random multiplier

Discard the decimal part. Limit the ordinary result to 1–9,999.

Defense removes an amount. Resistance then reduces what remains by a percentage. This order is why a 20% loss of defense does not always mean 20% more damage.

Attack power and defense

Attack power and Defense are calculated values. They combine a character’s class, current attributes, equipment, and battle conditions.

Physical attacks use physical attack power against physical defense. Damaging magic uses magic attack power against magic defense.

Class coefficients and editor names
Class coefficient Short name Used to calculate
Physical Attack Coefficient PAtk Coef Physical attack power
Magic Attack Coefficient MAtk Coef Magic attack power
Physical Defense Coefficient PDef Coef Physical defense
Magic Defense Coefficient MDef Coef Magic defense

A class coefficient is one input to the formula, not the completed attack power or defense. It is separate from the class’s starting attributes and gains per level.

Physical attack power

Physical attack power = Physical Attack Coefficient + Weapon STR bonus 6
× STR + Nonweapon equipment STR bonuses + 50 50
× DEX + Equipment DEX bonuses + 100 100
× Attack condition multiplier

Discard the decimal part after the complete calculation.

Physical defense

Physical defense = Physical Defense Coefficient 20
× VIT + Equipment VIT bonuses + 25 25
× STR + Equipment STR bonuses + 100 100
× Defense condition multiplier

Discard the decimal part after the complete calculation.

STR contributes to both physical attack power and physical defense. DEX helps physical attack power; VIT helps physical defense.

Magic attack power

Magic attack power = Magic Attack Coefficient + Equipment INT bonuses 6
× INT + 50 50
× MEN + Equipment MEN bonuses + 100 100
× Magic attack condition multiplier

Discard the decimal part after the complete calculation.

Magic defense

Magic defense = Magic Defense Coefficient 20
× MEN + Equipment MEN bonuses + 25 25
× INT + Equipment INT bonuses + 100 100
× Defense condition multiplier

Discard the decimal part after the complete calculation.

INT and MEN each contribute to both magic attack power and magic defense.

Use the character’s current attributes.

Level gains and temporary effects such as Poison change the attributes used here. Equipment bonuses are then added where the formulas show them.

A level-1 Amazon has a Physical Defense Coefficient of 20, STR 50, and VIT 45. Her default Short Bow adds 3 STR. With a condition multiplier of 1.00, physical defense is 4. The worked example shows each step.

The resulting attack power can receive further adjustments for a particular action or target. That adjusted value enters the main damage formula.

How Alignment changes power and defense

Virtue and Bane attacks use Alignment in physical or magic power and defense. The attack’s element selects the rule.

Virtue adjustment = (Alignment − 50) / 10
Bane adjustment = (50 − Alignment) / 10
Condition multiplier = (100 + Other bonuses + Alignment adjustment − Fatigue penalty) / 100

Add this adjustment once. Wind, Flame, Earth, and Water attacks instead compare their element with the character’s stored Element. Terrain and movement contribute separately.

Use the attacker’s Alignment for power and the target’s Alignment for defense. Both use the same attack element.

For a Virtue attack, Alignment 70 gives +2. With other bonuses and fatigue at zero, the multiplier is (100 + 2) / 100 = 1.02.

This multiplies power or defense by 1.02. It does not add two damage points directly.

A hypothetical damage example

Suppose power before this multiplier is 100, and defense before its multiplier is 50. Both characters have Alignment 70.

Use a Virtue attack. Set other bonuses, fatigue, Luck difference, and total resistance to zero. Use a random multiplier of 1.00.

Attack power = 100 × 1.02 = 102
Defense = 50 × 1.02 = 51
Damage = (102 − 51) × 1.00 × 1.00 = 51 HP

With both Alignment adjustments at zero, the same example gives 50 HP damage. These are hypothetical inputs, not a particular class matchup.

The adjustment keeps fractional tenths. Power, defense, and the final ordinary amount each discard decimals at their own calculation step.

See Alignment: combat calculations for the adjustment ranges.

Luck, resistance, and variation

Luck difference

The attacker’s total combat Luck is compared with the defender’s. Higher Luck adds to damage before resistance and random variation apply.

Luck difference =
(Attacker’s Luck + Attacker’s equipment Luck)
− (Defender’s Luck + Defender’s equipment Luck)

A difference of +5 adds 5 at this stage. A difference of −5 subtracts 5. Permanent Luck gains from earlier levels are already part of the character’s Luck.

Elemental resistance

Elemental resistance applies after defense. The game uses the defender’s resistance to the attack’s element, including when a physical attack uses an element.

How resistance changes the remaining damage
Resistance Amount retained
0 100%
20 80%
50 50%
80 20%

Resistance is limited to 0–100. At 100, the multiplication produces zero, then the ordinary calculation applies its minimum result of 1. Special effects and failed success checks have separate rules.

Random variation

The random multiplier ranges from 0.90 to 1.10. It changes the amount by up to 10% in either direction before the decimal part is discarded. The possible outcomes are not necessarily equally frequent.

How elemental resistance is built

Start with the target’s class resistance. Add resistance from its equipment and the applicable Element or Alignment adjustment.

For Wind, Flame, Earth, and Water, a matching target Element adds 4 resistance points. The opposing Element subtracts 4.

Wind opposes Earth. Flame opposes Water. Other pairings add zero.

Virtue and Bane use the target’s Alignment instead. This is separate from the defense adjustment described above.

Limit the combined resistance to 0–100 before applying it. Healing skips this resistance step.

Virtue resistance = Class + Equipment + (Target Alignment − 50) / 10
Bane resistance = Class + Equipment + (50 − Target Alignment) / 10

Worked example: Fighter against Amazon

A level-1 Fighter hits a level-1 Amazon with a Short Sword. At a random multiplier of 1.00, the hit deals 10 HP damage. Here is how the game reaches that result.

This calculated matchup uses the US retail class table’s level-1 attributes and default equipment. Your characters can have different attributes because of level gains and class changes.

1. Set up the attack

The Fighter stands in the front row. The Amazon stands in the rear row. Both units fight on Plain terrain with fatigue 0. Neither character has Poison or another temporary effect.

Calculate one successful, ordinary hit. For this example, the separate double-damage check does not activate. The Amazon starts at her full 65 HP.

Retail class values used for the level-1 matchup
Class value Fighter · attacker Amazon · defender
Level 1 1
Starting HP 70 65
STR 50 50
VIT 50 45
DEX 45 52
Luck 50 50
Physical Attack Coefficient 50 48
Physical Defense Coefficient 20 20
Class Physical resistance 45 48

Use the Fighter’s STR, DEX, and Physical Attack Coefficient for this hit. Use the Amazon’s VIT, STR, and Physical Defense Coefficient for her defense. The Amazon’s attack coefficient does not enter the calculation.

2. Add the actual equipment

Both characters use their class’s default equipment. The following table lists the relevant bonuses and the Bandanna’s separate MEN bonus.

Default equipment and bonuses for the Fighter and Amazon
Character Equipment Bonuses
Fighter Short Sword +3 STR; Physical element
Fighter Chain Mail +5 Physical resistance
Fighter Round Shield +2 Physical resistance
Fighter Iron Helm +2 Physical resistance
Amazon Short Bow +3 STR; Physical element
Amazon Leather Armor +3 Physical resistance
Amazon Bandanna +1 Physical resistance; +2 MEN

The Amazon has no item in her off-hand slot. None of this equipment adds DEX, VIT, or Luck. The Bandanna’s MEN bonus does not affect this physical hit.

A weapon’s STR bonus has two different uses.

The Fighter’s Short Sword adds 3 beside his class attack coefficient. The Amazon’s Short Bow adds 3 to the STR factor in her defense. Do not add the sword’s 3 twice when calculating the Fighter’s attack power.

3. Calculate the battle conditions

Plain terrain gives both characters a terrain adjustment of zero. The Fighter’s front-row physical attack adds 5 percentage points. The Amazon’s formation row does not add to her defense.

Neither character has a fatigue penalty, a typed Spellbook, or an applicable class or equipment condition bonus. Thus, the only condition adjustment is the Fighter’s +5.

Attack condition multiplier = (100 + 5 − 0) ÷ 100 = 1.05

Defense condition multiplier = (100 + 0 − 0) ÷ 100 = 1.00

4. Calculate the Fighter’s attack power

Each factor in the Fighter's physical attack power
Factor Substitution Meaning
Class coefficient and weapon (50 + 3) ÷ 6 50 from Fighter; +3 from Short Sword
STR factor (50 + 0 + 50) ÷ 50 = 2 STR 50; no STR bonus from other equipment
DEX factor (45 + 0 + 100) ÷ 100 = 1.45 DEX 45; no equipment DEX bonus
Condition factor 1.05 The front-row bonus calculated above

Physical attack power = ((50 + 3) ÷ 6) × 2 × 1.45 × 1.05

≈ 26.8975 → 26 attack power

Keep the fractions during multiplication. Discard the decimal part only after the complete attack-power calculation. The class coefficient of 50 has now produced attack power 26; neither number is HP damage.

5. Calculate the Amazon’s defense

Each factor in the Amazon's physical defense
Factor Substitution Meaning
Class coefficient 20 ÷ 20 = 1 Amazon’s Physical Defense Coefficient is 20
VIT factor (45 + 0 + 25) ÷ 25 = 2.8 VIT 45; no equipment VIT bonus
STR factor (50 + 3 + 100) ÷ 100 = 1.53 STR 50; +3 STR from Short Bow
Condition factor 1.00 No defense condition adjustment

Physical defense = 1 × 2.8 × 1.53 × 1.00

≈ 4.284 → 4 defense

Discard the decimal part after the complete defense calculation. The armor’s Physical resistance has a separate job in the next step.

6. Calculate Luck and resistance

Both characters have Luck 50, and their equipment adds no Luck. The Luck difference is therefore (50 + 0) − (50 + 0) = 0.

The Short Sword deals Physical damage. Use the Amazon’s Physical resistance, including her armor and Bandanna:

Physical resistance = 48 + 3 + 1 = 52

Amount retained = (100 − 52) ÷ 100 = 0.48

The class supplies 48, Leather Armor supplies 3, and Bandanna supplies 1. Thus, 48% of the amount left after defense and Luck reaches the random-variation step.

7. Convert the result into HP loss

Use a random multiplier of 1.00 for the first calculation. This is one possible roll, not a guarantee for every hit.

Final damage calculation, one stage at a time
Stage Calculation Result
Start with attack power 26 26
Subtract defense 26 − 4 22
Add Luck difference 22 + 0 22
Apply Physical resistance 22 × 0.48 10.56
Apply random variation 10.56 × 1.00 10.56
Discard the decimal part 10.56 → 10 10 HP damage
Subtract damage from current HP 65 − 10 55 HP left
(26 − 4 + 0) × 0.48 × 1.00
= 10.56 → 10 55 HP left

The ordinary damage limit does not change 10. If the separate double-damage check activates, this calculated 10 becomes 20 damage instead.

8. Allow for different rolls

Random variation for the same Fighter hit
Random multiplier Before discarding decimals Damage Amazon’s HP left
0.90 10.56 × 0.90 = 9.504 9 HP 56
1.00 10.56 × 1.00 = 10.56 10 HP 55
1.10 10.56 × 1.10 = 11.616 11 HP 54

With these conditions, an ordinary successful hit deals 9–11 HP before any double damage. These outcomes need not be equally frequent.

A Fighter has two front-row attacks. The example calculates one hit; the game checks each attack separately. Two hits need not have the same result.

The fatigue example and Poison example below reuse these same characters and equipment.

Fatigue

Fatigue weakens physical and magic attack power, both forms of defense, accuracy, and evasion. The first penalty begins at fatigue 70.

Fatigue penalty thresholds
Fatigue Penalty Multiplier*
0–69 0 1.00
70–79 5 0.95
80–89 18 0.82
90 or more 40 0.60

*When the other battle condition bonuses total zero.

The attacker and defender use their own fatigue. The penalty enters the condition multiplier alongside the applicable battle bonuses.

Attack condition multiplier = 100 + Physical attack condition bonuses − Fatigue penalty 100
Magic attack condition multiplier = 100 + Magic attack condition bonuses − Fatigue penalty 100
Defense condition multiplier = 100 + Defense condition bonuses − Fatigue penalty 100

Battle bonuses include terrain and movement interactions, certain equipment or class interactions, and formation for attacks. Magic attack conditions also include a weapon and attack-element interaction.

At fatigue 90 with other bonuses of +20, the multiplier is (100 + 20 − 40) ÷ 100 = 0.80. Fatigue does not simply multiply every completed value by 0.60.

Example: the Amazon becomes tired

Return to the Fighter against Amazon example. Keep the Fighter fresh, attack power 26, resistance 52, equal Luck, and random multiplier 1.00.

The Amazon’s defense before its condition multiplier is about 4.284. Apply fatigue to this value before discarding decimals.

Fatigue changes the Amazon's defense and damage taken
Amazon’s fatigue Defense calculation Defense Damage calculation
0–69 4.284 × 1.00 → 4 4 (26 − 4) × 0.48 → 10 HP
70–79 4.284 × 0.95 → 4 4 (26 − 4) × 0.48 → 10 HP
80–89 4.284 × 0.82 → 3 3 (26 − 3) × 0.48 → 11 HP
90 or more 4.284 × 0.60 → 2 2 (26 − 2) × 0.48 → 11 HP

At fatigue 70, her defense calculation decreases, but it still becomes 4 after rounding. Thus, this particular hit still deals 10 HP. At fatigue 80, defense becomes 3 and the hit deals 11 HP.

What if the Fighter is tired?

At fatigue 90, his front-row condition multiplier is (100 + 5 − 40) ÷ 100 = 0.65. His attack power becomes 25.6167 × 0.65 ≈ 16.6508, then 16.

Against the fresh Amazon, damage is (16 − 4) × 0.48 = 5.76, then 5 HP. If both characters have fatigue 90, damage is (16 − 2) × 0.48 = 6.72, then 6 HP.

Reducing fatigue

Power Fruit removes 20 fatigue. Angel Fruit removes 50. Neither can reduce fatigue below zero. Soldiers start battle with no fatigue penalty.

Poison Cloud

Poison Cloud is the Earth spell in the standard T3 group used by Witches. T3 means “Elemental Tier 3 Spell Template”; it is a spell group, not a character level.

Its weakness effect reduces all seven attributes: STR, VIT, INT, MEN, AGI, DEX, and Luck. With no other temporary attribute adjustment:

Attribute while poisoned = Original attribute × 0.90

Discard the decimal part. This version assumes no other temporary attribute adjustment.

An attribute of 100 becomes 90; an attribute of 99 becomes 89. These weakened attributes feed the attack power, defense, accuracy, and evasion calculations. Separate equipment bonuses are added later.

Example: the Amazon has Poison

Use the same Fighter and Amazon, both with fatigue 0. Poison changes the Amazon’s STR from 50 to 45, VIT from 45 to 40, and Luck from 50 to 45.

The VIT calculation is 45 × 0.90 = 40.5, which becomes 40. Her Short Bow still adds 3 STR. Her equipment and class still give Physical resistance 52.

Physical defense = (20 ÷ 20) × ((40 + 0 + 25) ÷ 25) × ((45 + 3 + 100) ÷ 100) × 1.00

≈ 3.848 → 3 defense

Luck difference = 50 − 45 = +5

Damage = (26 − 3 + 5) × 0.48 × 1.00 = 13.44 → 13 HP

The same hit now deals 13 HP instead of 10. Poison reduced both defense and Luck; the extra damage is not simply a 10% increase.

If the poisoned Amazon also has fatigue 90, her defense becomes 3.848 × 0.60 = 2.3088, then 2. Damage becomes (26 − 2 + 5) × 0.48 = 13.92, then 13 HP. Rounding can hide a further change for one particular hit.

Other temporary effects

Poison subtracts ten percentage points from the temporary attribute adjustment. A separate +10% adjustment and Poison’s −10% weakness cancel each other.

Attribute while poisoned =
Original attribute + Original attribute
× (Other temporary attribute adjustment − 0.10)

Multiply the adjustment by the original attribute, then add the original attribute. Discard the decimal part.

The calculation always starts from the original attributes. Reapplying Poison does not keep multiplying an already weakened attribute by 0.90.

Poison and fatigue can apply together.

Poison reduces attributes. Fatigue reduces condition multipliers. Poison does not raise the fatigue value or directly reduce equipment bonuses, class coefficients, or elemental resistance.

Accuracy and evasion

Accuracy and Evasion feed a separate success check. Higher accuracy helps the attacker pass it; higher evasion makes success less likely.

Both use AGI and DEX, equipment, fatigue, and applicable battle conditions. Poison also weakens them by reducing AGI and DEX.

Defense reduces the damage amount. Evasion affects the success check. A character can have high defense and low evasion.

A failed success check does not always mean zero damage. Some damaging magic can deal half the calculated amount. Status effects and special attacks have their own success rules.

Special attacks and healing

Physical, magic, and special attacks

An attack’s element and its damage formula are separate choices. A Virtue special attack does not necessarily use magic power.

Ordinary physical attacks use STR-based power. Certain beast and dragon attacks use DEX-based physical power. Both subtract physical defense.

Ordinary spells use INT-based magic power and subtract magic defense. Combined spells calculate each caster’s power before combining it.

In the alternate physical formula below, equipment bonuses include all equipped items. Discard decimals after the complete power calculation.

Alternate physical power =
(Physical Attack Coefficient + Equipment DEX) / 6
× (DEX + 50) / 50
× (VIT + Equipment VIT + 100) / 100
× Physical attack condition multiplier

Attacks that change the ordinary amount

Some actions change power before defense. Others replace or scale the amount afterward. These operations do not produce the same result.

For example, doubling power 50 before defense 20 gives 80. Doubling the remaining amount instead gives 60.

The success check and final HP rules still follow these calculations. Failed damaging spells and special attacks can halve the resulting amount.

ActionSpecial calculation
Mirage Slash; Fatal DanceMultiply incoming power by 1.5 before subtracting defense.
Tempest; Annihilation; Meteor Strike; White MuteHalve the computed integer amount before the 1–9,999 limit.
Wind StormMultiply the computed integer amount by 0.8. Discard decimals, then apply the 1–9,999 limit.
Throw a Kiss, both variantsUse one twentieth of the user’s current HP. Discard decimals, then apply the 1–9,999 limit.
Pumpkin Smash; Pumpkin ShowerUse half the target’s current HP. Discard decimals, then apply the 1–9,999 limit.

Double damage and failed attacks

Basic physical attacks and Shoot can double their calculated amount after a separate Luck check. Equipment Luck does not enter this check.

The threshold is 5 plus half the attacker’s Luck advantage. Discard decimals in that half, toward zero.

A random value from 0 through 99 must be below the threshold. A threshold of zero or less cannot succeed.

Physical attacks can miss for no HP damage. The checked damaging-spell paths instead halve their amount when the success check fails.

That halved spell amount is limited to 1–9,999 before the target’s HP rules apply.

Double-damage threshold = 5 + trunc((Attacker Luck − Target Luck) / 2)

Spells cast without a weapon

A missing-weapon bug can greatly change magic power. It applies when the calculation finds no item classified as a weapon.

The game reads outside its normal weapon-and-element table. The resulting bonuses enter magic power before defense is subtracted.

Bane receives +93 percentage points. Virtue receives −36. With all other bonuses and fatigue at zero, their power multipliers are 1.93 and 0.64.

These are not final damage multipliers. Stats, equipment, defense, Luck, resistance, and the action’s other rules still apply.

Vampires have no weapon slot in the normal class data. Their normal Life Drain uses alternate physical power, so it does not receive this magic-power bonus.

Assigning ordinary spells to a Vampire can expose the bug. Such a test changes its normal actions.

Angel Knights, Vultans, and Wizards have weapons in their default equipment. Equal class coefficients therefore do not guarantee equal magic power.

Spell elementMissing-weapon addition
Physical−65
Wind0
Flame+16
Earth+8
Water+7
Virtue−36
Bane+93

Combined spells

The game calculates each caster’s power against each target. With two casters, A is the higher power and B is the lower power.

Three-caster spells have a power-rearrangement bug. Call the first two powers lo and hi, from lower to higher. Call the third power Z.

A, B, and C below mean the resulting positions. They do not always mean highest, middle, and lowest power.

For powers 78, 130, and 104 in that order, the game uses 104, 78, and 78. Their sum is 260, not 312.

This can affect three-Cleric Healing as well as damaging spells. The first caster still supplies Luck; rearranging powers does not change that caster.

The spell and target position select a formula using A, B, and C. For example, an anchor can use A + B + C.

Some outer targets receive less incoming power. One rule halves the finished amount instead, which can turn a result of 1 into zero.

Unity changes the combination chance. It is not an extra damage multiplier.

Third powerABC
Z ≤ lohiloZ
lo < Z ≤ hiZlolo
Z > hiZhilo

Healing

Healing uses the caster’s magic power and subtracts the recipient’s magic defense. Luck difference and random variation still apply.

Healing skips elemental resistance. Do not multiply it by the recipient’s Virtue resistance.

Virtue Alignment adjustments still affect power and defense. With other inputs equal, higher caster Alignment increases healing.

Higher recipient Alignment increases magic defense and reduces healing received. Reducing Magic Defense can therefore increase healing received.

For example, suppose magic power is 120, magic defense is 80, and Luck difference is zero. With no random change, healing is 40.

If magic defense falls to 50, the same calculation gives 70. The recipient only gains as much HP as it is missing.

Healing Plus and combined healing can use different amounts at different target positions. Ordinary Healing does not revive dead characters.

Ordinary Healing amount = clamp(trunc((Magic power − Magic defense + Luck difference) × Random multiplier), 1, 9999)
HP restored = no more than the recipient’s missing HP

Clamp means keep the result between 1 and 9,999. Apply this limit before the recipient’s HP capacity.

A result of zero or −20 becomes 1 before capacity. A combined outer-target rule can then halve 1 to zero.

Soldier attacks

Each Soldier member makes a success check. The number of successful members sets a multiplier on physical power before defense.

For 0 through 9 successful members, the multipliers are 0, 0.6, 0.8, 1, 1.3, 1.6, 2, 2.3, 2.6, and 3.

Discard decimals after multiplying power. A separate Soldier support calculation also exists; its exact availability remains unconfirmed.

Other attack rules

Pumpkin attacks use half the target’s current HP. A failed success check halves that amount again. The minimum calculated amount is 1.

Earthquake skips characters with Sky movement unless they are petrified, paralyzed, or asleep.

Healing and Healing Plus restore no HP to Zombies, Skeletons, or Ghosts. Vampires are not in that excluded group.

Healing cannot restore lost Soldier members. It stops at the HP limit of the surviving members.

Gaze and other status-only actions can change a status without causing HP damage. Damage-triggered class changes have separate requirements.

Life Drain and recoil

Life Drain first calculates its attack amount. If its success check fails, halve that amount and limit it to 1–9,999.

The user’s recovery starts from that calculated amount, not the target’s actual HP loss. Recovery cannot exceed the user’s missing HP.

For example, an amount of 40 against a target with 10 HP can restore up to 40 HP. The target loses only 10.

Sonic Boom causes recoil after its target effects. Recoil is one sixth of the user’s alternate physical power for the secondary calculation.

Discard decimals and limit Sonic Boom recoil to 1–9,999. Target defense and resistance do not reduce this recoil.

Pumpkin Shower also causes recoil after its target effects. Use half the user’s current HP at that point, discard decimals, and limit it to 1–9,999.

Recoil reduces the user’s HP and can kill the user. At 1 HP, Pumpkin Shower still causes 1 recoil damage.

From calculated amount to HP change

The calculated amount and the final HP change can differ. The target cannot lose more current HP than it has.

Some actions drain HP into the attacker or cause recoil. Those second effects have their own calculations and recovery limits.

Attack counts describe how many actions a character takes from each row. They do not multiply the damage of one action.

The technical reference records uncommon battle conditions and internal amount choices whose player-facing triggers are not yet established.

See Unity: target area and power for combination examples.

Battle glossary

These are the same definitions that open from the formula links.

The damage calculation

Damage

The calculated HP loss from an attack. Current HP stops at zero.

Attack power

The strength calculated for an attack before defense, Luck, elemental resistance, and random variation apply. Physical attacks and magic use different attributes.

Defense

The calculated amount subtracted from attack power. Physical attacks use physical defense; magic uses magic defense.

Luck difference

The attacker’s Luck and equipment Luck bonuses, minus the defender’s equivalent total. The result can be positive or negative.

Elemental resistance

The target’s class resistance, equipment resistance, and Element or Alignment adjustment, limited to 0–100. It reduces the amount after defense and Luck. Healing skips resistance.

Random multiplier

A factor from 0.90 through 1.10 that varies the ordinary damage result. The possible outcomes are not necessarily equally frequent.

Discard the decimal part

Keep the whole-number part of the result. The game does this after calculating each complete attack power or defense value and after the ordinary damage multiplication.

The 1–9,999 limit

The ordinary damage result cannot be lower than 1 or higher than 9,999. This bound belongs to the ordinary calculation. Special effects, double damage, and failed success checks have separate rules.

Attributes

STR — Strength

Contributes to ordinary physical attack power and physical defense. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

VIT — Vitality

Contributes to physical defense. Some special attacks can also use it. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

INT — Intelligence

Contributes to magic attack power and magic defense. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

MEN — Mentality

Contributes to magic attack power and magic defense. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

AGI — Agility

Contributes to accuracy and evasion. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

DEX — Dexterity

Contributes to ordinary physical attack power, accuracy, and evasion. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

LCK — Luck

Contributes to ordinary damage and separate Luck-dependent checks. Use the current combat attribute, before adding separate equipment bonuses. Poison’s weakness applies to this attribute.

Class coefficients

Class coefficient

One of four fixed class values used to calculate physical or magic attack power and defense. Class coefficients are separate from base attributes, growth per level, and attack counts.

Physical Attack Coefficient

A fixed class value that enters the physical attack power formula. The editor labels it PAtk Coef. It is neither completed attack power nor a percentage.

Magic Attack Coefficient

A fixed class value that enters the magic attack power formula. The editor labels it MAtk Coef. Equipment INT bonuses are added to it in the first part of the formula.

Physical Defense Coefficient

A fixed class value that enters the physical defense formula. The editor labels it PDef Coef. Divide it by 20 before applying the attribute and condition factors.

Magic Defense Coefficient

A fixed class value that enters the magic defense formula. The editor labels it MDef Coef. Divide it by 20 before applying the attribute and condition factors.

Equipment and battle conditions

Weapon STR bonus

The STR bonus from the first recognized weapon in equipment-slot order. It enters the first part of the ordinary physical attack power formula. With no weapon, this term is zero.

Nonweapon equipment STR bonuses

The combined STR bonuses from equipped items that are not weapons. The physical attack formula uses this term separately from the weapon’s STR bonus.

Equipment STR bonuses

The sum of the Strength bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment DEX bonuses

The sum of the Dexterity bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment INT bonuses

The sum of the Intelligence bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment MEN bonuses

The sum of the Mentality bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment VIT bonuses

The sum of the Vitality bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment AGI bonuses

The sum of the Agility bonuses from all four equipped items. Add these bonuses where the formula shows them. Poison does not directly reduce the bonuses themselves.

Equipment Luck bonuses

The combined combat Luck bonuses from the four equipped items. These are added to the character’s Luck for ordinary damage. They are separate from permanent Luck gains received at a level increase.

Attack condition multiplier

The physical attack factor for battle conditions. Add the applicable bonuses, subtract the attacker’s fatigue penalty, add 100, then divide by 100.

Magic attack condition multiplier

The attack condition factor for magic. It includes the physical attack condition components plus the weapon and attack-element interaction. It uses the attacker’s fatigue.

Defense condition multiplier

The condition factor used by both physical and magic defense. It uses the defender’s applicable battle bonuses and fatigue penalty. Formation is not part of this defense factor.

Status and success

Fatigue

A character’s fatigue value determines a penalty to attack power, defense, accuracy, and evasion. The first penalty begins at 70. Poison does not increase this value.

Fatigue penalty

Subtract 0 for fatigue below 70, 5 for 70–79, 18 for 80–89, or 40 for 90 and above. The attacker and defender use their own fatigue.

Poison Cloud

The Earth spell in the standard T3 group used by Witches. Its weakness effect reduces STR, VIT, INT, MEN, AGI, DEX, and Luck by 10% when no other temporary attribute adjustment applies.

Accuracy

The attacker’s calculated value for an attack’s success check. AGI, DEX, equipment, fatigue, and applicable battle conditions affect it. Higher accuracy helps the attack succeed.

Evasion

The defender’s calculated value for the success check. Higher evasion makes success less likely. It is separate from defense, which reduces the damage amount.

Formula factors and constants

100: the percentage scale

A full amount is 100%. Dividing by 100 converts a percentage into a multiplier.

Physical attack power

The attack power used by ordinary physical attacks. It combines the class’s Physical Attack Coefficient, STR, DEX, equipment, and attack conditions.

Magic attack power

The attack power used by ordinary damaging magic. It combines the class’s Magic Attack Coefficient, INT, MEN, equipment, and magic attack conditions.

Physical defense

The amount subtracted from a physical attack’s power. It combines the class’s Physical Defense Coefficient, VIT, STR, equipment, and defense conditions.

Magic defense

The amount subtracted from a magic attack’s power. It combines the class’s Magic Defense Coefficient, MEN, INT, equipment, and defense conditions.

Attacker’s Luck

The attacking character’s current LCK attribute before separate equipment Luck bonuses. Permanent gains from previous levels are already included.

Defender’s Luck

The defending character’s current LCK attribute before separate equipment Luck bonuses. This value and the defender’s equipment Luck are subtracted in the Luck difference.

Physical attack condition bonuses

The sum of applicable terrain and movement, attack-element matchup or Alignment, formation, anti-dragon, and same-side leader or monster-affinity bonuses. Each component can depend on the combatants and attack.

Magic attack condition bonuses

The physical attack condition bonuses plus the interaction between the weapon and the attack’s element. Add the components before applying the condition multiplier.

Defense condition bonuses

The defender’s terrain and movement, attack-element matchup or Alignment, anti-dragon, and same-side leader or monster-affinity terms. Some terrain conditions can add a further bonus. Formation and weapon/attack-element bonuses are excluded.

Original attribute

The character’s attribute before the current temporary attribute adjustments. Use the character’s value after level gains, not the class’s starting value.

Attribute while poisoned

The combat attribute after Poison’s weakness effect. With no other temporary adjustment, take 90% of the original attribute and discard the decimal part.

Other temporary attribute adjustment

The total of temporary attribute changes apart from Poison. Express it as a decimal in the full weakness formula: +10% is +0.10. Poison subtracts 0.10 from this adjustment.

0.10: Poison’s reduction

Poison subtracts ten percentage points from the temporary attribute adjustment. The game recalculates from the original attribute, so repeated applications do not keep multiplying the weakened value by 0.90.

0.90: the amount retained

With Poison alone, the character keeps 90% of each original attribute. Separate equipment bonuses are added later.

6: attack scaling

A fixed divisor in both ordinary attack power formulas. Divide the combined class coefficient and specified equipment bonus by 6 before multiplying by the other factors.

20: defense scaling

A fixed divisor in both defense formulas. Divide the class defense coefficient by 20 before multiplying by the attribute and condition factors.

50: the attack attribute scale

A fixed number used in the leading attribute factor for ordinary attack power. Add 50 to the indicated attribute and bonuses, then divide by 50.

100: the secondary attribute scale

A fixed number used in the second attribute factor. Add 100 to the indicated attribute and equipment bonuses, then divide by 100.

25: the defense attribute scale

A fixed number used in the leading defense attribute factor. Add 25 to VIT or MEN and its equipment bonuses, then divide by 25.

Modder reference: Damage

Choose the part of the calculation you want to change: action routing, class scaling, elemental conditions, or final amount handling. An action's element and its physical or magic score family are separate inputs.

What do you want to change or understand?

Where do I start when one attack is too strong?

Identify its stored mode and amount selector first. Then follow the selected score builder into the amount kernel.

Start with Stored action records · Choose physical or magic power · Attack and defense score builders

Why does the same spell behave differently with different equipment?

Check weapon recognition and the weapon/action element table. Missing weapons reach an unchecked table row in the magic context.

Start with Weapon-element lookup · Stored element adjustment tables

Why does Healing vary between recipients?

Healing bypasses final resistance, but retains the recipient's defense and its conditions. The ordinary amount limit is another separate step.

Start with Healing skips final resistance · Alignment in attack conditions · Ordinary amount limits

How to read the source and byte evidence

ROM offsets use big-endian z64 order. The master v64 stores each byte pair in reverse order. RAM addresses belong to the stated overlay or structure.

Each code line shows z64 offset, four original bytes, and MIPS assembly. Relative branches name z64 destinations; J/JAL targets are encoded RAM addresses. The next instruction is the branch delay slot.

Samples are stored bytes, not calculated outputs. Decoded resources have separate container and decoded-offset labels. Repository paths identify local sources; this page needs no external files.

Healing skips final resistance

Which part of defense does Healing bypass?

Primary effect D3=2 causes the combined evaluator to set kernel flag bit 0. The kernel then clears final resistance. It still calculates defense, Luck, and the amount, so resistance zero does not mean defense zero.

Start here: Trace D3 from the action through the evaluator's flag argument, then inspect magic defense for recipient differences.

Stored or calculated?
D3 is stored metadata. The flag and resistance result are computed call inputs and outputs.

This excerpt proves one bypass, not every healing rule. HP capacity still limits the later applied recovery.

Ordinary amount limits

Why does the calculated amount differ from the HP change?

The ordinary kernel limits its result to 1 through 9999. Later executor rules can halve, double, redirect, or cap that amount. Current HP and missing HP impose separate limits at application.

Start here: Check the kernel result, then the action executor and its HP application call. Keep those three values separate.

Stored or calculated?
The amount is computed. The bounds are code constants, not a per-action amount table.

COMBAT SYSTEMS

Accuracy & evasion

Why attacks hit, why they fail, and why the game shows GUARD! or MISS!

The main rules

This guide explains the ordinary physical-hit check in the US retail version of Ogre Battle 64.

  • AGI, DEX, and Luck all affect the chance to avoid a normal physical attack.
  • The attacker and defender both matter. A character has no fixed dodge percentage against every opponent.
  • GUARD! and MISS! can show the same failed hit check. The defender’s class selects the label.
  • The label selection makes no second guard or dodge roll.
  • Fatigue can reduce accuracy and evasion. Equipment and some battle conditions also affect them.

Start with the explanations and example. Use the full formulas when you want to calculate a result.

GUARD! and MISS!

When this physical-hit check fails, the defender avoids the attack. The game then selects a message from the defender’s class setting.

MessageExample defender classes
GUARD!Fighter, Knight, Ninja, Sword Master
MISS!Amazon, Wizard, Archer, Ghost

A Ninja can attack a Ghost and get MISS!. The same Ninja can attack a Sword Master and get GUARD!.

The different words do not show which defender has better evasion. Neither word proves that another defensive roll occurred.

This guide uses avoid the attack for either result. A separate DODGE message is not verified for this path.

Which attributes help

The attacker performs the attack. The defender is its target.

AttributeWhen this character attacksWhen this character defends
AGI: AgilityRaises accuracyRaises evasion
DEX: DexterityRaises accuracyRaises evasion
LCK: LuckRaises the hit thresholdLowers the attacker’s hit threshold

Accuracy and evasion are calculated scores. Neither score is a percentage.

More DEX can therefore help a defender avoid an attack. AGI is not the only evasion attribute.

The gain depends on both characters, their conditions, and rounding. Ten extra points in an attribute do not promise ten percentage points of improvement.

Defense reduces the damage calculation. Evasion affects the hit check. A character can have high defense and low evasion.

Use current attributes and add equipment once

  1. Start with the character’s current combat AGI, DEX, and Luck.
  2. Use any changes from Poison or another temporary attribute effect.
  3. Add the separate equipment bonuses shown in each formula.

Add together the relevant bonuses from all four equipped items. If your supplied values already include those bonuses, do not add them again.

How the hit check works

  1. Calculate the attacker’s accuracy.
  2. Calculate the defender’s evasion.
  3. Use both scores, the Luck difference, and the battle-side adjustment to calculate the hit threshold.
  4. Compare a roll from 0 through 99 with that threshold.
Roll below the hit threshold: the attack passes the hit check.
Roll equal to or above the threshold: the defender avoids the attack.

For example, a threshold of 75 accepts rolls 0 through 74. Rolls 75 through 99 fail.

Hit thresholdAccepted roll valuesHit percentageAvoid percentage
0None0%100%
750 through 7475%25%
1000 through 99100%0%

These percentages assume that all 100 roll values are equally likely. They describe a chance, not a promised result over 100 attacks.

There is no completed hit followed by another dodge roll in this path. The comparison above decides whether this hit check passes.

A separate double-damage check can change damage after a successful check. It does not choose between GUARD! and MISS!.

Ninja example

A Ninja attacks a Sword Master. Each character’s current attributes are chosen for this example.

InputNinja: attackerSword Master: defender
AGI100150
DEX100100
Luck5050
Equipment AGI, DEX, and Luck bonuses00
Fatigue00
Applicable leader bonus00

Use Plain terrain, which gives an evasion terrain adjustment of 0. Neither character has a temporary status effect.

Step 1: Calculate accuracy

Accuracy = (100 + 50) × ((100 + 100) / 55) × 1.00
         ≈ 545.45
         → 545 after discarding the decimal part

Step 2: Calculate evasion

Evasion = (150 + 50) × ((100 + 100) / 50) × 1.00
        = 800

Step 3: Compare the scores and Luck

Before the battle-side adjustment:

truncate((545 / 800) × (100 + 50 − 50))
= truncate(68.125)
= 68

The game adds either 0 or 10 for the attacker’s battle side. This example shows both results.

Battle-side adjustmentHit thresholdHit percentageAvoid percentage
06868%32%
+107878%22%

With threshold 68, roll 67 passes. Roll 68 fails, and this Sword Master shows GUARD!.

A Ghost uses MISS! for the equivalent failed check. The message choice does not make another roll.

Change one value

Keep the Ninja unchanged. Change only the listed Sword Master value from the example.

ChangeEvasionAvoid: side adjustment 0Avoid: side adjustment +10
Example values80032%22%
Defender AGI rises to 200100046%36%
Defender DEX rises to 150100046%36%
Defender Luck rises to 6080039%29%
Defender fatigue rises to 904800%0%

In this example, more AGI and more DEX both help. Ten extra Luck raises the avoid percentage by seven percentage points.

At fatigue 90, evasion falls to 480. The calculated hit threshold reaches its limit of 100.

Rounding can hide a small attribute change. Keep the opponent and battle conditions fixed when you compare results.

Full formulas

These formulas apply when the ordinary physical-hit calculation is used. Read the special cases below before applying them to other attacks.

Truncate means discard the decimal part. Keep fractions during each calculation and truncate only at the marked steps.

1. Attacker accuracy

Accuracy = truncate(
    (attacker DEX + attacker equipment DEX + 50)
    × ((attacker AGI + attacker equipment AGI + 100) / 55)
    × ((100 + attacker leader bonus − attacker fatigue penalty) / 100)
)

2. Defender evasion

Evasion = truncate(
    (defender AGI + defender equipment AGI + 50)
    × ((defender DEX + defender equipment DEX + 100) / 50)
    × ((100 + defender terrain adjustment
            + defender leader bonus − defender fatigue penalty) / 100)
)

3. Hit threshold

Luck difference =
    attacker Luck + attacker equipment Luck
    − defender Luck − defender equipment Luck

Hit threshold = limit to 0–100(
    truncate((Accuracy / Evasion) × (100 + Luck difference))
    + battle-side adjustment
)

Limit to 0–100 means replace results below 0 with 0, and results above 100 with 100.

4. Simple percentages

Hit percentage   = Hit threshold
Avoid percentage = 100 − Hit threshold

These percentages count accepted and rejected roll values. They do not measure a separate dodge roll.

The game uses limited numerical precision. A hand calculation near a rounding boundary can differ from the game.

The battle-side adjustment

The battle-side adjustment is 0 or +10. Add it after truncating the score-and-Luck result, then apply the 0–100 limit.

Its assignment to the player or enemy is not confirmed for every battle setup. Do not assume that the player always receives +10.

This is a separate term from the class leader affinity bonus.

Fatigue and terrain

Fatigue

Each character uses their own fatigue penalty. The first penalty starts at fatigue 70.

FatiguePenaltyScore multiplier when all bonuses are 0
0 through 6901.00
70 through 7950.95
80 through 89180.82
90 or more400.60

Fatigue reduces the attacker’s accuracy and the defender’s evasion. It enters before the completed score loses its decimal part.

With an applicable leader bonus of +15 and fatigue 80, the accuracy condition multiplier is:

(100 + 15 − 18) / 100 = 0.97

The Sword Master and Ninja in the example do not receive that leader affinity bonus. The next section lists the qualifying classes.

Terrain

The terrain adjustment depends on the defender’s class movement type and the battle terrain. Its value ranges from −5 through +3.

Plain terrain gives 0 for each normal movement type. Other terrain can help one movement type and hinder another.

Terrain enters the evasion formula shown here. It does not enter this attacker accuracy formula.

An exact calculation on other terrain needs the applicable terrain adjustment. This guide does not include the full terrain lookup.

Poison

Poison Cloud’s weakness effect reduces the combat attributes used in these formulas. Its effect can combine with fatigue.

Use the resulting combat AGI, DEX, and Luck. Add the separate equipment bonuses afterward.

Class leader affinity

Class leader affinity is a bonus for certain leader and member classes on the same battle side.

Choose the leader’s row and the member’s group. Use that one value as the character’s leader bonus in both score formulas.

The table applies when the game’s leader and character-state checks allow the bonus. Some special states can suppress it.

Leader classListed beastsGolemsListed dragonsOther listed monsters
Beast Tamer †+10+10+10+10
Doll Master †0+10+10+10
Dragon Tamer00+10+10
Beast Master+15+10+10+10
Enchanter0+15+10+10
Dragon Master †00+15+10
Vampire †000+10
Saturos †000+10
Daemon †000+15
Other leader classes0000

Classes in each member group

Use these exact lists. A group name in this table does not include other classes with a similar name or appearance.

Member groupIncluded classes
Listed beastsWyrm, Wyvern, Griffin, Opinincus, Cockatrice, Sphinx, Hellhound, Cerberus
GolemsGolem, Stone Golem, Baldr Golem
Listed dragonsYoung Dragon, Thunder Dragon, Red Dragon, Earth Dragon, Blue Dragon, Platinum Dragon, Black Dragon, Quetzalcoatl, Flarebrass, Ahzi Dahaka, Hydra, Bahamut, Tiamat
Other listed monstersGorgon, Gremlin, Goblin, Ogre

Member classes outside these lists receive 0 from this class rule.

What +10 and +15 mean

With no fatigue or terrain adjustment, +10 gives a score multiplier of 1.10. A bonus of +15 gives 1.15.

These values increase the applicable accuracy or evasion score. They do not directly add 10 or 15 percentage points to the final chance.

For example, Beast Tamer gives a qualifying Wyrm +10. Beast Master gives that Wyrm +15.

Dragon Tamer gives a qualifying Young Dragon +10. Dragon Master gives that Young Dragon +15.

Do not add bonuses from different leader rows. The game selects one leader for this check.

† Class versions with the same name

Some class versions share a name but have different results in this lookup. The name alone does not prove that a bonus applies.

Additional versions named Beast Tamer, Doll Master, Dragon Master, Vampire, Saturos, and Daemon return 0 when checked as leader classes.

An additional Gorgon version also receives 0 as a member. The table includes both checked Beast Master versions and both checked Enchanter versions.

The visible identities of all these special versions still need confirmation. This limit matters when you compare named or special characters.

Special cases

  • Magic: Do not apply the physical-hit outcome to every spell. Some failed magic checks reduce damage instead of preventing it.
  • Soldiers and disabled targets: These can use extra rules or bypass the ordinary calculation.
  • Special attacks and battle states: These can change the normal result.
  • DODGE: No separate DODGE message was found in the shared combat result graphics examined for this path.

The GUARD!/MISS! distinction is verified for the ordinary physical-attack path described here. It does not classify every failed action in the game.

For damage after a successful hit, read the Damage guide. For combined magic, read the Unity and combined spells guide.

Guide glossary

Attacker

The character that performs the attack.

Defender

The character targeted by the attack.

AGI: Agility

A character attribute that contributes to both accuracy and evasion.

DEX: Dexterity

A character attribute that contributes to both accuracy and evasion. It also contributes to ordinary physical attack power.

LCK: Luck

The attacker’s Luck and the defender’s Luck affect the hit threshold. Add each character’s separate equipment Luck bonuses once.

Accuracy

The attacker’s calculated score for the hit check. It is not a percentage.

Example: Accuracy 545 must still be compared with the defender’s evasion.

Evasion

The defender’s calculated score for the hit check. A higher score makes an ordinary physical hit less likely.

Hit threshold

A whole number from 0 through 100. The attack passes the check when its random roll is below this number.

Example: A threshold of 75 accepts rolls 0 through 74.

Roll

The final random whole number used for this comparison. It ranges from 0 through 99.

Example: At a threshold of 75, roll 74 passes and roll 75 fails.

Percentage in this guide

The share of the 100 possible roll values that gives a result. This assumes that each roll value is equally likely.

Example: A threshold of 75 accepts 75 roll values and rejects 25. It does not guarantee 75 hits in every 100 attacks.

Equipment bonus

The sum of the relevant bonuses from all four equipped items. Add AGI bonuses to AGI, DEX bonuses to DEX, and Luck bonuses to Luck.

Class leader affinity bonus

A bonus for certain leader and member classes on the same battle side. Use the class leader affinity table. The bonus enters both accuracy and evasion.

Example: An applicable +15 bonus adds 15 inside the score’s condition calculation. It does not guarantee 15 more percentage points of success.

Terrain adjustment

A value from −5 through +3, selected from the character’s movement type and the battle terrain. It enters evasion in this calculation.

Battle-side adjustment

The game adds either 0 or 10 to the attacker’s hit threshold before the 0–100 limit. Its player/enemy assignment is not confirmed for every battle setup.

Truncate: discard the decimal part

Keep only the whole-number part. Do this at the marked steps.

Example: 68.9 becomes 68. A value of −3.9 becomes −3.

Limit to 0–100

Use 0 for a result below 0. Use 100 for a result above 100. Keep other results unchanged.

Modder reference: Accuracy and evasion

For hit balance, follow accuracy score, evasion score, threshold, and final comparison in that order. For GUARD! versus MISS!, use the separate class label table.

What do you want to change or understand?

How do I make a class harder to hit?

Compare its current AGI, DEX, equipment, terrain, fatigue, and leader conditions. Evasion is computed against an attacker's score, not stored as one class percentage.

Start with Defender evasion score · Evasion terrain matrix · Score ratio, Luck and threshold clamp

Where does a changed hit formula take effect?

The score ratio and Luck produce a bounded threshold. The physical executor then accepts rolls strictly below that threshold.

Start with Attacker accuracy score · Score ratio, Luck and threshold clamp · Final roll comparison

Can I change GUARD! without changing evasion?

The class reaction byte selects the failed-hit label after the check. It does not provide a defensive bonus.

Start with GUARD!/MISS! class lookup

How to read the source and byte evidence

ROM offsets use big-endian z64 order. The master v64 stores each byte pair in reverse order. RAM addresses belong to the stated overlay or structure.

Each code line shows z64 offset, four original bytes, and MIPS assembly. Relative branches name z64 destinations; J/JAL targets are encoded RAM addresses. The next instruction is the branch delay slot.

Samples are stored bytes, not calculated outputs. Decoded resources have separate container and decoded-offset labels. Repository paths identify local sources; this page needs no external files.

Defender evasion score

Why does defender DEX affect avoidance as well as AGI?

Evasion multiplies AGI plus 50 by the DEX factor using divisor 50. Terrain, leader affinity, and fatigue then adjust the score. A stronger defender score lowers the later accuracy/evasion ratio.

Start here: Read defender conditions alongside this builder, then compare both scores in hit-threshold.

Stored or calculated?
Evasion is computed for the current defender and battle conditions, not stored as a class dodge rate.

Evasion terrain matrix

Movement selects a row and effective battle terrain selects a column. In the first-row sample, FF means -1, FE means -2, and FB means -5. The value enters evasion conditions before truncation.

COMBAT SYSTEMS

Unity & combined spells

Choose the right spells. Bring the casters together. Give the combination a chance.

Unity helps a squad cast combined spells. Two or three casters can join their spells into one result. The recipe determines what they cast and which positions it can affect.

High Unity improves the chance, not the damage.

Unity 99 always passes the Unity check. The casters must still be ready, share a target, and have a valid recipe.

Set up a combination

  1. Choose a combination from the recipe list.
  2. Use the class-row table to select the required spell groups.
  3. Equip spellbooks that produce the required elements.
  4. Use a tactic that directs the casters toward the same target.
  5. Keep the casters together as a starting formation, then check whether they act together.

All participating casters must be ready when the battle system groups them. A valid recipe alone does not guarantee a combination.

The Leader tactic has produced a combination in a recorded battle where Strongest split the casters’ targets. This is a useful setup choice, not a guarantee.

Same-line formations are a useful starting point. A complete position-by-position rule for visible formations is not yet established.

What Unity changes

Unity belongs to the squad, rather than to an individual caster or a particular pair. A successful combination does not spend it.

The game draws a whole-number roll from 0 through 99. The Unity check passes when:

Roll ≤ Unity

A roll equal to Unity passes.

The usual percentage is:

Chance ≈ smaller of (Unity + 1) and 100, expressed as a percentage
UnityChance of passing the Unity check
0About 1%
25About 26%
50About 51%
75About 76%
98About 99%
99 or 100Certain

Unity 50 accepts 51 roll values: 0 through 50. Unity 0 can still pass on a roll of 0. The percentages are approximate because the random roll values are not perfectly equally frequent.

Increasing and protecting Unity

ChangeEffect
Flag of UnityAdds 1–5, with a maximum of 100
A qualifying battle resultAdds 5, with a maximum of 99
Remove one ordinary nonleader memberResets the squad’s Unity to 0
Cast a combined spellDoes not spend or increase Unity

The exact battle-result condition for the +5 gain is not identified. Do not count on every victory adding Unity.

A Flag of Unity is not sold in normal retail shop lists. A reliable normal-play source for the item is not established.

Save before changing a squad whose Unity you want to preserve. The effects of leader removal and other squad changes are not fully known.

There is no established Unity gain from waiting, travel, or simply keeping the same members together. The game has no confirmed normal numeric display for this value.

Which spell will a caster use?

Start with the class and formation row. These select the spell group. Equipment then selects an element for a standard elemental spell.

Class + formation row → spell group
Spell group + element → Actual spell

T1, T2, and T3 are guide labels for spell groups. They are not character levels. Higher Unity does not turn T1 into T2.

ElementT1T2T3
WindLightningThunder FlareShock Bolt
FlameFireballFire StormRay of Paralysis
EarthAcid VaporCrag PressPoison Cloud
WaterIce BlastIce FieldSlumber Mist
VirtueHealingHealing PlusNone
BaneWord of PainDark QuestNightmare

These are the 17 spells accepted as combination ingredients. A caster using T3 with Virtue casts ordinary Healing, so there is no eighteenth spell.

Spellbooks take priority

For a standard elemental spell group, a spellbook takes priority over the weapon. Book of Flame selects Flame even when the weapon has a different element.

A plain Spellbook uses the caster’s assigned element. If no spellbook is equipped, the first weapon can supply the element.

Tempest, Annihilation, Meteor Strike, and White Mute do not combine. Summons, elemental Blast attacks, Ignis Fatuus, and physical attacks are also outside these spell recipes.

Find a recipe

Select the spells the casters will actually use. Add a third spell to see whether all three contribute or the game keeps a pair.

Lightning

Lightning + Lightning forms a two-caster spell with a five-position cross.

The recipe finder checks spell compatibility. Readiness, formation grouping, the shared target, and the Unity check still apply.

Two-caster combinations

The game accepts 48 pairs. Caster order does not change the result.

Within one element, T1 + T1 gives T1. T1 + T2 and T2 + T2 give T2. Two T3 spells of the same element do not combine.

The six cross-element families are Wind + Flame, Wind + Water, Flame + Earth, Earth + Water, Wind + Bane, Flame + Bane. T3 spells work only with their exact listed T3 partner.

What a third caster changes

A third caster can increase power, change the result, or be left out. Do not add all three powers until the recipe confirms three participants.

Three T3 spellsKeep all three for the element check

The remaining elements are checked next. One element or a compatible cross-element family can keep all survivors. Incompatible groups can reduce three candidates to a matching pair.

If three distinct elements remain, the game selects a preferred pair or rejects the selection. The selected pair must still match an exact recipe.

Target area and power

The selected target position is the center of the spell’s area. It is not necessarily the center of the enemy formation.

Side positions are directly above, below, left, and right. Diagonal positions are the four corners. The game skips empty, out-of-bounds, or otherwise invalid positions.

Calculate power separately for each target

Calculate each participating caster’s magic attack power against the target. A, B, and C are the resulting power positions.

A pair puts its higher power in A and lower power in B. Three casters can trigger a bug that discards the highest score.

For powers 78, 130, and 104 in that order, the game uses A = 104, B = 78, and C = 78.

Use the three-caster rearrangement table before applying the formulas below.

CombinationAreaSelected targetSide positionsDiagonal positions
Pair, except T2 + T2CrossA + BDiscard decimals from (A + B) ÷ 4Not included
T2 + T2 pairSquareA + BA + whole-number part of B ÷ 2Discard decimals from (A + B) ÷ 2
T1/T2 trio with fewer than two T2 spellsCrossA + B + CDiscard decimals from (A + B + C) ÷ 2Not included
Trio with at least two T2 spells, or a true T3 trioSquareA + B + CA + B + whole-number part of C ÷ 2Discard decimals from (A + B + C) ÷ 2

These expressions give incoming power, not damage. Apply the target’s magic defense, Luck difference, resistance, and random multiplier afterward.

Damage = (Combined power for a target − Magic defense + Luck difference) × (100 − Elemental resistance) ÷ 100 × Random multiplier

Discard the decimal part, then apply the ordinary 1–9,999 limit. See Damage for the full calculation.

Luck comes from the Source caster and the target, including their separate equipment bonuses. Adding caster powers does not add all participants’ Luck together.

A wider spell still checks defense.

Every valid target uses its own defense and resistance. A pair reduced from three candidates uses the pair rules. Healing and status combinations are not all HP-damage attacks.

One unusual recipe is Acid Vapor + Ice Blast + Ice Field. It produces Blue Spiral with the five-position trio rule. The recipe finder includes this exception.

Worked example: two Wizards cast Fireball

When two eligible Wizards combine Fireball, the result is still named Fireball. Its five-position cross and combined power make it different from an ordinary single-caster Fireball.

1. Choose the spells and values

Both Wizards use their plain Spellbook’s Flame element and stand in the middle row. Wizard uses T1 there, so each caster supplies Fireball.

Use INT 55, MEN 61, and Luck 50 for each Wizard. These are the Wizard class-table values. Your current characters can differ because of their growth and class history.

Wizard inputValue or equipment
Magic Attack Coefficient53
INT / MEN / Luck55 / 61 / 50
Scipplay Staff+3 INT
RobeNo INT or MEN bonus
Spellbook+1 INT; caster’s Flame element
Amulet+4 INT
Total equipment INT3 + 1 + 4 = 8

Both Wizards are fresh and fight on Plain terrain. The middle row adds no formation adjustment. The Flame attack matching the caster’s stored Flame element adds 4 percentage points; the other applicable adjustments are zero.

2. Calculate each caster’s power

Magic attack condition multiplier = (100 + 4 − 0) ÷ 100 = 1.04

Magic attack power = ((53 + 8) ÷ 6) × ((55 + 50) ÷ 50) × ((61 + 0 + 100) ÷ 100) × 1.04

≈ 35.7484 → 35 per Wizard

A = 35; B = 35

3. Apply the target-area rule

Fireball + Fireball is a T1 pair. The selected target receives power 35 + 35 = 70. Each valid side position receives the whole-number part of 70 ÷ 4 = 17.

4. Calculate damage to an Amazon

Use the level-1 Amazon and default equipment from the Damage example, with fatigue 0. Her MEN is 48 and INT is 45. Bandanna adds 2 MEN; her Magic Defense Coefficient is 23.

Magic defense = (23 ÷ 20) × ((48 + 2 + 25) ÷ 25) × ((45 + 0 + 100) ÷ 100) × 1.00

≈ 5.0025 → 5 defense

Her Flame resistance is 50, and the Luck difference is zero. Use a random multiplier of 1.00 and a successful effect check:

Amazon’s positionDamage calculationHP lost
Selected target(70 − 5 + 0) × 0.50 × 1.00 = 32.5 → 3232 HP
A side position(17 − 5 + 0) × 0.50 × 1.00 = 66 HP

These are alternative positions for an Amazon with the same values. A target receives the result for its own position, not both amounts.

Side damage is not one quarter of the final 32 damage. The game reduces incoming power first, then subtracts that side target’s defense.

Unity decides whether the eligible combination passes its check. It does not change either the 70 power or the 17 power.

When a combination does not happen

CheckWhat to look for
Spell choiceCheck the actual spells, not only class names or equipped weapons.
RecipeUse the finder. Some valid three-caster selections intentionally leave one caster out.
TargetMake the casters select one target. Try Leader when their target choices split.
ReadinessA disabled or mistimed caster can leave the eligible group.
FormationKeep the casters together as a starting setup; not every visible position is confirmed.
UnityEven a valid setup can fail this check below Unity 99.

Some details are still unknown. These include which battle results add 5 Unity, how each squad change affects Unity, and which formation positions can combine.

The recipe tables apply once the game selects eligible casters.

Unity glossary

Click a linked term anywhere in this article to open the same explanation.

Unity

One value shared by a squad. It controls the chance of passing the combined-spell check. It does not increase spell power or get spent when a combination succeeds.

Unity check

The game draws an integer from 0 through 99. The check passes when that number is equal to or below the squad’s Unity. Other combination requirements still apply.

Combined spell

A spell formed from two or three eligible casters. Their actual spells must match a recipe, and their squad must pass its Unity check.

T1, T2, and T3

Short names for three spell groups in this guide. They are not character levels. A class’s formation-row action selects the group; equipment can select its element.

Actual spell

The spell a caster will use after class, formation row, and equipment are considered. The recipe checks this spell, not the caster’s class name.

Recipe

An exact set of compatible spells and its combined result. A spell’s presence in the compatible list does not mean it combines with every other listed spell.

Shared target

The final participating casters must select the same target. A tactic can affect their choices. Passing the Unity check does not make different target choices match.

Flag of Unity

An item that adds a random 1–5 Unity to a squad, up to 100. Normal retail shop lists do not sell it. A reliable normal-play acquisition route is not established.

Spellbook priority

For a standard elemental spell group, the first equipped spellbook selects the element before any weapon can. A plain Spellbook uses the caster’s assigned element.

Three participating casters

All three selected spells survive the recipe checks. The three-caster power calculation can discard one score because of a bug. Three available casters do not always produce this result.

A third caster is left out

The game can select a compatible pair from three candidates. Only the retained pair contributes to the combined spell. Use the pair’s target area and power rules.

Selected target position

The position around which the spell’s target area is arranged. It receives the sum of the resulting power positions. It need not be the formation’s center.

Side position

A position directly above, below, left, or right of the selected target position. Its incoming power depends on the pair or trio recipe.

Diagonal position

One of the four corner positions around the selected target position. Only a nine-position combined spell includes these positions.

A — first resulting power

The first power after the game rearranges caster scores. In a pair it is the higher score. A three-caster bug can discard the highest score.

B — second resulting power

The second power after score rearrangement. In a pair this is the lower score. In a trio, use the rearrangement rules on the Damage page.

C — third resulting power

The third power after score rearrangement. It can duplicate the lower score because of a three-caster bug. A missing caster supplies zero before rearrangement.

Combined power for a target

The power passed into the ordinary magic calculation at one target position. It comes from the participating caster powers and the recipe’s area rule. It is not yet HP damage.

Source caster

The acting caster whose Luck enters the target’s ordinary effect calculation. Adding the participants’ attack powers does not add all their Luck together.

Modder reference: Unity and combined spells

Separate three questions: whether a combination attempt starts, which casters and spells remain compatible, and how their power is combined. Unity controls the first gate; it does not scale combined damage.

What do you want to change or understand?

How do I investigate combination frequency?

Start with the Unity comparison. A passed roll still needs eligible participants, compatible resolved spells, and a usable target.

Start with Unity combination check · Read a compatibility trie

Where would a new spell combination belong?

Follow element selection, category selection, and the output recipe in order. Each table can remove candidates before output selection.

Start with Stored recipe and selector tries · Read a compatibility trie

Why can three-caster damage look inconsistent?

Inspect the computed power rearrangement after compatibility. One retail branch duplicates the lower score rather than sorting correctly.

Start with Three-caster power rearrangement

How to read the source and byte evidence

ROM offsets use big-endian z64 order. The master v64 stores each byte pair in reverse order. RAM addresses belong to the stated overlay or structure.

Each code line shows z64 offset, four original bytes, and MIPS assembly. Relative branches name z64 destinations; J/JAL targets are encoded RAM addresses. The next instruction is the branch delay slot.

Samples are stored bytes, not calculated outputs. Decoded resources have separate container and decoded-offset labels. Repository paths identify local sources; this page needs no external files.

Unity combination check

Does Unity 50 mean exactly half the rolls pass?

The gate accepts roll <= Unity, so 50 accepts residues 0 through 50; zero still accepts zero. Canonical storage is persistent unit +0x0C, copied to active squad +0x1F. These are two representations of one value.

Start here: Read the comparison first, then participant and recipe checks. For progression, follow Flag use and battle-results writers in Combat Modes.

Stored or calculated?
Unity is stored; the roll and compatibility result are computed. It is neither consumed nor used as a damage multiplier.
Before you edit
Keep the persistent and active record origins distinct. Seven-bit save width alone does not establish safe custom gameplay values.
Inspect original source, bytes, and field layout

The unit Unity byte is compared with a random remainder0..99. A roll above Unity rejects the attempt; later eligibility checks still apply.

Read a compatibility trie

How do I follow a recipe table without flattening it incorrectly?

A trie stores paths of matching keys. The reader can retain an earlier nonzero result while following a longer path. A later zero result does not necessarily erase that retained selection.

Start here: Read key, retained result, and child offset together. Follow child offsets from that table's base, then inspect the output recipe.

Stored or calculated?
Four-byte stored selector records produce a computed participant selection.

Three-caster power rearrangement

What does the three-caster overwrite change?

After ordering the first two scores as hi and lo, the branch lo < third <= hi produces (third, lo, lo). For scores hi=100, lo=40, third=70, the result is (70,40,40). Caster identities do not move with these values.

Start here: Follow the resulting A/B/C values into the target's power selector in the damage calculation reference.

Stored or calculated?
These are temporary computed scores, not caster stats or recipe bytes.
Before you edit
A sorting correction changes retail behavior. It needs its own implementation and verification; rearranging recipe rows cannot repair these instructions.
Inspect original source, bytes, and field layout

This branch retains the overwrite instructions. If lo < third <= hi, the resulting powers are (third,lo,lo), not a correct descending sort.

Stored recipe and selector tries

Which of the three tables controls my intended combination?

Element and category selectors choose surviving participants; the output trie chooses the resulting spell. The first element record 01 00 00 1A means key 1, no replacement result, and child offset 0x001A. The output trie uses six-byte records instead.

CHARACTER & CAMPAIGN

Alignment

What Alignment does

Alignment runs from 0 to 100. Low values are Chaotic. High values are Lawful.

Each character has a current Alignment value. A class’s starting value is only the initial value for characters created from that class.

SystemWhat uses Alignment
Class changesA target class can require an inclusive minimum and maximum. Some automatic transformations also check Alignment.
Battle changesA credited kill can change the killer’s Alignment. Battle settlement can move eligible characters toward the player participants’ average.
Combat calculationsVirtue and Bane attacks use Alignment in power, defense, and resistance. Healing skips resistance.
Stronghold takeoversThe squad’s average affects the change to Chaos Frame.
Menus and presentationThe game displays Alignment, uses it for sorting, and selects some leader or scene profiles from it.
Lestat’s questionnaireThe visiting leader’s exact Alignment must be 0–49 to continue through additional entry conditions.

Individual Alignment, squad average Alignment, and [[ali-chaos|Chaos Frame]] are different values. A Lawful character does not guarantee a favorable stronghold result.

This guide covers the identified code paths in the US retail game. Some event activation details remain unconfirmed.

Ways it changes

AvenueResultImportant condition
Scroll of DisciplineRaises Alignment by 1, 2, or 3.The result stops at 100.
Urn of ChaosLowers Alignment by 1, 2, or 3.The result stops at 0.
A credited killAdds a calculated change from −5 through +5.Alignment difference, level difference, and the battle tactic contribute. Exclusions apply.
Battle settlementMoves eligible characters toward the player participants’ average by up to 3 points.This happens through the battle-result path. It is not proved to occur while merely waiting.
Character creationSets a starting value from class data.Starting-roster setup also has fixed overrides. This is initialization, not recurring growth.

The normal item and battle writers limit Alignment to 0–100. Near an endpoint, the actual change can be smaller.

At Alignment 99, a Scroll gives 100 for any of its three rolls. At Alignment 1, an Urn gives 0.

Goblet of Destiny changes Luck. Luck is a separate character value.

The checked level-growth writer does not raise Alignment with level. A class change does not imply a reset to the new class’s starting Alignment.

Creation, recruitment, and saved values

A newly created character receives a starting value. A successful neutral recruitment copies the recruited character’s existing Alignment into the player roster.

One prepared-roster setup sets two generated Fighters and one generated Amazon to Alignment 50. Their names are not fixed story-character names.

Loading a saved game restores the saved Alignment. Battle setup and result processing also copy values between the roster and temporary battle records.

Battle changes in detail

A credited kill

Use the killer and the defeated target’s current battle values. Calculate each difference as killer minus target.

kill change = Alignment-difference term + level-difference term + tactic term
Limit the change to −5 through +5.
Add it to the killer’s Alignment, then limit the result to 0–100.
Alignment differenceTerm
−100 to −76−5
−75 to −51−4
−50 to −26−3
−25 to −6−2
−5 to −1−1

Autonomous−1
