Autonomous selects a random target. Attack Strongest selects the greatest current HP. Attack Leader selects the leader.

Attack Weakest selects the greatest estimated damage. These terms affect the kill change, not every action performed under that tactic.

Example: Alignment 60 defeats Alignment 40 at the same level. The Alignment term is +2, and the level term is 0.

Attack Leader adds +1. The kill change is +3, so Alignment becomes 63 before later battle settlement.

A higher-level killer can lose Alignment. The level penalty can outweigh the Alignment and tactic terms.

Some combined-action paths apply this calculation to more than one credited participant.

The calculation excludes a Soldier as either the killer or the defeated target. It also excludes enemy-side killers.

Training disables both per-kill changes and average-based settlement. A separate scripted-scene state also preserves Alignment.

Gladiator Magnus, Warrior Dio, and Lord Destin are also excluded from the per-kill change. This exclusion does not apply to average-based settlement.

After the battle

The result path first calculates the average Alignment of player-side battle participants. It excludes Soldiers. Dead participants still contribute to this average.

Living player-side characters other than Soldiers then move toward that fixed average. Petrified characters contribute to the average but do not receive this change.

For surviving petrified characters, settlement restores the Alignment recorded at battle start.

Average minus current AlignmentChange
−100 to −51−3
−50 to −21−2
−20 to −6−1
−5 to 50
6 to 20+1
21 to 50+2
51 to 100+3

Example: Participants at 30 and 70 have an average of 50. Their changes are +1 and −1, producing 31 and 69.

A difference from −5 through +5 gives no drift. The game computes the average before applying these individual changes.

The battle result can therefore include a kill change and a later average-based change. Read the final character value after settlement.

Class requirements

A class requirement includes both endpoints. Meeting the Alignment range alone does not satisfy the class’s other requirements.

Target classAlignment range
Knight40–100
Phalanx20–80
Paladin60–100
Black Knight0–40
Archmage0–40
Princess70–100
Angel Knight50–100
Seraph75–100

A Paladin requirement of 60–100 accepts 60 and rejects 59. A Black Knight requirement of 0–40 accepts 40 and rejects 41.

Automatic transformation checks can also use Alignment. The post-scenario Angel Knight path requires Alignment 50–100 alongside other conditions and a random check.

Alignment 100 does not guarantee an Angel Knight transformation. The other gates still apply.

Combat power and defense

Virtue and Bane attacks use Alignment in attack power and defense. The attack’s element selects the rule.

Virtue adjustment = (Alignment − 50) ÷ 10
Bane adjustment = (50 − Alignment) ÷ 10
AlignmentVirtue adjustmentBane adjustment
0−5+5
30−2+2
5000
70+2−2
100+5−5

At Alignment 70, Virtue gets +2 and Bane gets −2. At Alignment 50, both terms are zero.

Use the attacker’s Alignment for attack power. Use the target’s Alignment for defense. Both use the same attack element.

Add each adjustment to that character’s other bonuses before applying the condition multiplier. Terrain and class movement contribute separately.

These are percentage-point adjustments inside power and defense. They are not direct damage points or a universal bonus for high Alignment.

Target Alignment also adjusts Virtue and Bane resistance by the same formulas. Higher Alignment gives more Virtue resistance and less Bane resistance.

Healing ignores resistance. Alignment still affects the healer’s magic power and the recipient’s magic defense.

With other inputs equal, higher healer Alignment increases healing. Higher recipient Alignment increases magic defense and reduces healing received.

See Damage: Alignment and Healing for the calculation order and examples.

The checked ordinary physical accuracy and evasion formulas have no Alignment term. Do not treat higher Alignment as a general hit or dodge bonus.

Strongholds and Chaos Frame

A player squad’s takeover compares its average Alignment with the stronghold’s morale. It changes Chaos Frame, not each member’s Alignment.

This average uses valid members in the squad’s five member slots. It uses current values, not the leader alone or class starting values.

score = absolute difference between squad average and site morale
      + site penalty, either 0 or 40
      + random whole number from 0 through 7
Final scoreChaos Frame change
0–5+2
6–15+1
16–300
31–50−1
51–80−2
81–110−3
111–140−4
141 or more−5

After the change, Chaos Frame remains within 0–100. Some sites have a no-change setting that bypasses this calculation.

A squad with average Alignment 50

  • At morale 50 with no site penalty, the score is 0–7. The result is +2 or +1 Chaos Frame.
  • At morale 90 with no site penalty, the score is 40–47. The result is −1 Chaos Frame.
  • At morale 50 with the 40-point site penalty, the score is also 40–47. The result is −1 Chaos Frame.

Match the squad’s average to the site when planning a favorable takeover. Simply making every squad more Lawful can worsen the comparison.

The site penalty is a separate setting. It must not be inferred solely from whether the site currently appears allied, enemy, or neutral.

Menus, speech, and events

Character displays and roster sorting read current Alignment. Item-selection checks can disable an Alignment item when the character is already at its limit.

Some leader presentation profiles use Alignment bands together with character type and special class overrides.

These profiles select contextual messages, including neutral-encounter lines. They also select the leader’s two lines of shop commentary.

The checked shop use changes flavor text. It does not establish an Alignment discount or different stock.

A scene-script query also combines character type with Alignment bands: 0–32, 33–65, and 66–100. Specific story classes override that result.

Ordinary profile before special-class overridesLow bandMiddle bandHigh band
Leader messages and shop commentary0–3435–6566–100
Scene-script profile0–3233–6566–100

These profile systems do not all use the same band boundaries. Do not substitute a displayed label for an exact class requirement or takeover calculation.

A separate event-property query can read the character’s exact Alignment. Its corresponding direct setter is absent from that property table.

Lestat’s Bloody Emblem questionnaire

One entry condition checks the visiting unit’s leader at Alignment 0–49. Alignment 50–100 bypasses the questionnaire branch.

Additional checks concern the leader’s class and character type, Bloody Emblem inventory quantity, and event state. Alignment alone does not guarantee the event.

The later success result can award a Bloody Emblem. Low Alignment permits the attempt; it does not guarantee success or award the item immediately.

The reward still needs inventory capacity. The event records completion before its final capacity check.

This route does not directly convert the leader into a Vampire. The complete activation requirements remain unconfirmed.

Neutral Talk

Current Alignment is not a direct input to the checked neutral Talk calculation. That path reads class behavior, HP, and a class-comparison result.

A different class can change those inputs. Do not confuse this class-based behavior with a check of the character’s current Alignment.

The neutral-encounter message profile can use Alignment even though the Talk success calculation has no direct Alignment term.

What remains unconfirmed

  • Story recruitment: The neutral Talk result does not establish every scripted recruitment condition.
  • Equipment: No direct equipment bonus to current Alignment is established here. Equipment can affect other values and class-related conditions.
  • Waiting and map movement: No change from elapsed time alone is established. The verified average-based change belongs to battle settlement.
  • Events and endings: Lestat’s questionnaire still needs its complete activation requirements traced. Chaos Frame effects remain separate from individual Alignment effects.
  • Scripted scenes: One preservation state has a verified code test but no complete list of triggering scenes.

These are limits of the evidence. They do not prove that an untraced route cannot exist.

Alignment glossary

Alignment

A character’s current position on the Chaotic–Lawful scale. The ordinary range is 0 through 100. Higher values are more Lawful.

Squad average Alignment

The sum of the included members’ current Alignment values, divided by their number. Discard the decimal part. Different systems have different inclusion rules.

Example: 40, 50, and 60 give an average of 50.

Chaos Frame

A separate army reputation value. A stronghold takeover can change it by comparing the squad’s average Alignment with the site’s morale.

Site morale

A stronghold value used in the takeover comparison. A separate site setting can add 40 to the comparison score.

Limit to a range

Replace a value below the minimum with the minimum. Replace a value above the maximum with the maximum.

Example: An Alignment result of 102 becomes 100. A result of −2 becomes 0.

Killer

The character credited with reducing the target to zero HP on a checked attack path.

Difference

Subtract the second value from the first. The order matters.

Example: Killer Alignment 60 minus target Alignment 40 gives +20.

Movement type

A property selected from the character’s class. Movement and battlefield terrain supply a separate combat adjustment. The attack’s element selects the Alignment adjustment.

Combat adjustment

A term in the attack-power or defense calculation. An extra point is not a promise of one extra point of damage.

Which Alignment rule changes damage or capture outcomes?

Virtue/Bane have separate power, defense, and resistance uses. Stronghold takeover instead reads unit mean Alignment and changes Chaos Frame.

Read current persistent Alignment

Which byte is the character's current Alignment?

The getter indexes a 56-byte roster record and reads its Alignment byte. Values 0 through 100 are ordinary; zero is valid Chaotic Alignment. This value is independent of Luck and the class starting value.

Start here: Use the roster record's +0x1B field, then follow battle-copy when inspecting a combat actor.

Persistent Alignment save descriptor

Why is the saved Alignment field not just a raw roster byte?

Descriptor bytes 1B 01 07 mean character offset 0x1B, one destination byte, and seven packed bits. The codec packs roster fields, so the RAM record layout cannot be used as direct save-file offsets.

Start here: Read the field descriptor with the roster-level count and stride contract, then use the existing save codec.

Stored or calculated?
Stored serialization metadata describes how current Alignment is packed and restored.
Before you edit
Seven bits can represent 0..127, but ordinary Alignment is 0..100. This excerpt does not validate a changed descriptor or save round trip.

The roster is 100 records of 56 bytes. Save descriptor triple 1B 01 07 identifies field offset, destination width, and packed bit width.

Scroll and Urn changes

Where do Scroll and Urn amounts come from?

The Scroll adds 1..3 and the Urn subtracts 1..3. Both reach a shared signed-delta application and 0..100 clamp. At the corresponding endpoint, availability rejects use before consuming an item.

Start here: Follow the item-specific random delta, shared application, and availability checks together.

Stored or calculated?
Current Alignment is stored; the selected delta and clamped result are computed by code.
Before you edit
Changing the application alone can leave menu availability inconsistent. The excerpt does not include the full random or item-selection path.

Scroll of Discipline adds 1..3; Urn of Chaos subtracts 1..3. The shared application clamps to 0..100 and stores through the rebased field pointer.

Credited killing-action Alignment delta

Which table would change Alignment gains from kills?

Separate ordered tables convert attacker-minus-target Alignment and level differences into signed steps. The Alignment sample 4C 05 means a minimum difference of 76 gives +5. Tactic adds another step before delta and final-value clamps.

Start here: Choose the relevant contribution table, preserve its comparison direction, then inspect the caller that credits the killing action.

Stored or calculated?
Stored signed threshold/step pairs feed a computed delta limited to -5..+5.

Post-battle convergence

Why does a non-killer's Alignment change after battle?

Results compute one participant mean, then adjust eligible survivors toward it. The sample 33 03 means a mean-minus-current difference of at least 51 gives +3. The mean stays fixed while recipients update.

Start here: Check who contributes to the mean separately from who receives a change, then inspect the signed threshold table.

Stored or calculated?
The mean and each change are computed; seven stored pairs control the step sizes.
Before you edit
Dead and petrified participants can enter the mean but do not receive convergence. Recomputing the mean after each update would change the rule.

Results move eligible participants toward a fixed participant mean using seven threshold/step pairs. This precedes experience presentation.

Virtue/Bane power context

How do I change Alignment's contribution to spell power?

Virtue adds (Alignment-50)*0.1 to conditions; Bane reverses the difference. The sample is a double-precision 0.1 constant, not a stored per-class bonus. Current caster Alignment supplies the variable.

Start here: Trace the action-element branch and condition result into the power builder. Check recipient defense independently.

Stored or calculated?
Stored Alignment feeds computed conditions; the multiplier is a code constant.
Before you edit
Movement is a separate input. Changing this term does not change the target's independent final resistance rule.
Inspect original source, bytes, and field layout

Virtue adds (caster Alignment-50)*0.1; Bane reverses it. The saved value in the movement-call delay slot is the preceding action element.

Final resistance and Healing bypass

The kernel combines class, equipment, and target-Alignment resistance terms, then clamps resistance. Flag bit 0 overrides that finished resistance to zero. Standard Healing sets this flag but retains defense conditions.

CHARACTER & CAMPAIGN

Automatic class changes

When class changes happen

Automatic class changes happen at three different times. Each uses its own requirements.

WhenPossible changes
After battle resultsDragons, several beasts, and Angel Knights can evolve. Soldiers can graduate through a separate check.
During an attackCertain attacks can change Golems and undead.
After scenario completionEligible dead characters can become Angel Knights or Zombies.

Manual class changes and transformation items are not covered here.

After-battle evolution

The game checks evolution after battle results. A character does not need to gain a level in that battle.

It checks class, stats, Alignment, and Element. There is no chance roll.

A minimum means that value or higher. An Alignment range includes both ends. For example, 25–75 includes both 25 and 75.

The Element column checks the stored Wind, Flame, Earth, or Water value. No spellbook item is required. “Any” means any value passes.

Training does not allow these evolutions. Dead characters, petrified characters, enemies, and Soldiers cannot receive them.

A character can evolve only once during this check. It cannot immediately evolve again into the next class.

Evolution keeps current HP, maximum HP, six stats, level, Luck, and Alignment. It does not heal the character or reset stats.

The new class changes the character’s actions and appearance. Equipment can still look unchanged during the battle.

After battle, default equipment changes to the new class’s defaults. Items you explicitly selected remain selected.

Which Young Dragon change takes priority?

The game checks Platinum Dragon first, then Black Dragon. It checks the four elemental dragons next, in table order.

At Alignment 70–75, Platinum Dragon wins if its requirements pass. At Alignment 25–30, Black Dragon wins if its requirements pass.

Example: A Young Dragon has Wind, every stat at 200, and Alignment 70. It becomes a Platinum Dragon.

For an elemental dragon, meet that row’s requirements without meeting an earlier row’s requirements.

Angel Knight to Seraph

Current classNew classMinimum statsAlignmentElement
Angel KnightSeraphIntelligence 108; Mentality 125; Dexterity 12175–100Any

Seraph also requires Needle of Light, Baldr Mail, and Kite Shield to be available.

  • An item that is part of the current class’s default equipment counts.
  • An item this character already wears also counts.
  • Otherwise, you need an unequipped spare.

Each required item must still have an inventory entry, even when it counts as default or worn equipment.

An ordinary Angel Knight already has the required Needle of Light and Kite Shield. Keep spare Baldr Mail unless that character already wears it.

Checking availability does not use up an owned item. Plate Mail can still appear during the evolution animation.

After battle, default armor changes to Seraph’s Baldr Mail. That copy of Baldr Mail then counts as equipped.

Armor you explicitly selected remains selected instead. For example, explicitly selected Plate Mail stays equipped.

Becoming an Angel Knight after scenario completion has a different rule. It requires three unequipped spares, even if the dead character wears those items.

Soldier graduation

After battle results, a Soldier formation can be replaced by a new Fighter or Amazon. This is called graduation.

No level gain is required. The new character gets newly generated stats, not the Soldier’s old stats.

Earning graduation progress

The unit leader keeps the graduation progress. A qualifying battle result adds two points for each surviving, nonpetrified Soldier member.

In ordinary battles, the result qualifies when only your side can still fight. It also qualifies when both sides survive but yours receives less damage.

Special battle rules can change that result. Graduation can use progress already earned; it does not require new points from that battle.

A carried Medal of Vigor doubles the gain. Three qualifying Soldier members give six points, or twelve with the Medal.

How the game counts surviving Soldiers

1. Divide the formation’s maximum HP by 3. Round down.
   This is the HP share for one Soldier.
2. Divide its current HP by that share. Round up.
   Count no more than 3 surviving Soldiers.
3. Add the surviving counts from all qualifying formations.
4. Multiply that total by 2 for progress.
   With Medal of Vigor, double it again.

This calculation assumes the normal maximum HP is at least three. Round down means discard the fraction; round up means count the next whole number.

Reaching 100 progress

At 100 progress, the game checks whether graduation can happen. You need fewer than 94 occupied character records and spare starter equipment.

If a later requirement fails, progress becomes 99. Successful graduation resets it to zero.

Training and neutral encounters block graduation. Some formation and scripted conditions also block it.

Fighter or Amazon

A standard Fighter leader produces a Fighter. A standard Amazon leader produces an Amazon. A carried Ansate Cross reverses those choices.

The game uses the leader’s character type for this choice. Special character types have not been individually mapped here.

ResultRequired starter equipment
FighterShort Sword, Chain Mail, Round Shield, Iron Helm
AmazonShort Bow, Leather Armor, Bandanna

You need an unequipped spare of every listed item. The graduate equips those items; your total owned quantities do not decrease.

The new character’s stats

The new level comes from the scenario’s shared Soldier starting data. It does not come from the old Soldier’s current level.

The game generates a name and new stats. The graduate starts at full HP, with Luck 50 and Alignment 50.

“Base” is the level-1 value. “Growth” is the guaranteed increase for each additional level.

StatFighter base / growthAmazon base / growth
HP70 / 465 / 3
Strength50 / 350 / 3
Vitality50 / 245 / 1
Intelligence40 / 245 / 2
Mentality46 / 248 / 2
Agility42 / 150 / 2
Dexterity45 / 252 / 2
Start with the base value at level 1.
For each additional level:
  Add the listed growth.
  Add a random 0 or 1, twice using separate rolls.
  Stop at 999 if the result would exceed it.

For example, one Fighter Strength increase adds three, four, or five points. Starter equipment adds no extra growth through the checked fields.

After growth, Luck is set back to 50. The game randomly chooses one of the four stored values used by the Element column.

Experience, fatigue, status, and graduation progress start at zero. The new character uses default equipment without custom equipment selections.

The game also records the remaining Soldier members. The traced code does not establish that they return to Soldier Reserves.

Changes caused by attacks

Certain attacks can change Golems and undead during battle. There is no level or Alignment requirement, and no separate transformation roll.

The attack must still succeed normally. A damaging attack must leave the target alive and not petrified. A killing blow prevents the change.

Current classNew classMinimum base statsRequired attack
GolemStone GolemStrength 104; Vitality 129Gaze of Terror, Petrify, or a physical hit with Ji’ylga’s Bow
Stone GolemBaldr GolemStrength 144; Vitality 185Plasma Ball or Plasma Storm
ZombieSkeletonNoneFlame damage
SkeletonGhostNonePlasma Ball or Plasma Storm

Base stats here exclude equipment bonuses. Training blocks these changes. Some scripted conditions also block them.

Golem to Stone Golem

Gaze of Terror must pass its normal success and petrification checks. A qualifying Golem changes class instead of becoming petrified.

Petrify must hit, and the Golem must survive. Its separate roll to cause petrification does not need to succeed.

Ji’ylga’s Bow needs a successful physical hit that the Golem survives. No separate petrification roll is required.

Undead changes

Flame damage includes Fire Breath, Crimson Note, Fireball, Fire Storm, Salamander, and Fire Blast. Flame weapon hits can also cause the Zombie change.

For these changes, Plasma means Plasma Ball or Plasma Storm. Ordinary Wind lightning does not count.

Ray of Paralysis and Bind Flare do not count just because their element matches. They cause different effects.

Your Zombie normally needs Halt Hammer and Torn Cloth available to become Skeleton. Default equipment and items already worn count; otherwise, provide spares.

A Skeleton with default equipment already has Ghost’s required Torn Cloth. Golems need no new equipment.

Enemy characters skip the inventory check. Checking availability does not use up an item.

What changes and what stays

The character keeps remaining HP, maximum HP, level, six base stats, Luck, Alignment, name, and identity.

The change replaces custom equipment with class defaults. Special named characters can use defaults tied to their retained identity.

After-battle evolution instead keeps custom equipment selections.

Changes after scenario completion

After scenario rewards, eligible dead characters may become Angel Knights or Zombies. This does not happen after every battle.

The game checks dead characters in roster order. Unit leaders cannot transform. The character does not have to be in a deployed unit.

Ordinary eligible classes are Fighter and the human classes from Amazon through Centurion. Soldier, Lycanthrope, Angel Knight, and existing undead classes are excluded.

Some special versions of classes also qualify. Named characters can keep their identity while changing class.

CharacterFirst checkIf it fails
Eligible femaleAngel Knight requirements and chance rollA fresh Zombie roll
Eligible maleZombie rollNo transformation

Angel Knight: 1. Check spare equipment

The dead character must be an eligible female who is not a unit leader. Keep one unequipped copy of each item:

  • Needle of Light.
  • Plate Mail.
  • Kite Shield.

Items worn by the dead character do not count as spares. Other characters’ equipment does not count either.

Earlier characters in roster order can take spares before later characters are checked.

Angel Knight: 2. Check stats and Alignment

  • Intelligence: at least 60.
  • Mentality: at least 61.
  • Dexterity: at least 57.
  • Alignment: 50 through 100.

These are permanent character stats. There is no level, Strength, Vitality, or Agility requirement for this change.

Angel Knight: 3. Roll for success

Once the equipment and stat requirements pass, Luck sets the chance. Divide Luck by four to get the approximate percentage.

Chance (%) ≈ Luck ÷ 4

Example: Luck 40 gives about a 10% chance, not 40%. Passing every requirement allows the roll; it does not guarantee an Angel Knight.

Exact roll

The game generates a number from 0 through 32,767. It divides that number by 400 and keeps the remainder.

The remainder must be less than Luck. With Luck 40, remainders 0–39 pass; 40 and higher fail.

Exact test: random number % 400 < Luck
The % sign means “remainder after division.”

The remainders are not equally common across all 32,768 possible numbers. Luck 40 passes for 3,280 of them, which is slightly above 10%.

Angel Knight: 4. If it fails

Missing equipment, insufficient stats, or a failed Luck roll can lead to a fresh Zombie roll. It is a separate chance.

A successful Angel Knight change skips the Zombie roll entirely.

Zombie chance and protection

An eligible male goes straight to the Zombie roll. An eligible female reaches it when the Angel Knight attempt fails.

The Zombie chance is about 30%. The game divides a new random number by 10 and accepts remainders 0, 1, or 2.

Exact Zombie test: random number % 10 < 3
After the roll passes, the character must also be unprotected.

Mastaba’s Barrier protects members of its unit from becoming Zombies. It is not used up and does not block Angel Knight creation.

Angel’s Brooch is not checked for either of these death changes.

A storage bug can also protect a paired roster slot outside the Barrier’s unit. Do not treat this as normal extra item coverage.

After a successful death change

The character keeps name, level, experience, maximum HP, six permanent stats, Luck, and Alignment. Current HP returns to maximum.

Custom equipment selections are cleared. The new class uses its default equipment. Most old equipment returns to the unequipped inventory.

Sonic Blade, Hemlock, Dream Tiara, Blue Sash, and Tunic are exceptions among eligible class defaults. You lose those copies when they are removed.

Custom equipment follows the same internal item rule. Some other items can also be lost that way.

Angel Knight equips the three spare items. A Zombie gets Old Clothing.

If you have no Old Clothing and every inventory slot is occupied, the clothing cannot be added.

The character stays in the roster. You do not need a free character slot.

Existing undead recover HP

At scenario end, a separate check fully heals Zombies, Skeletons, and Ghosts in roster slots 1–94. It does not change their class.

Scope and remaining questions

  • Some scripted conditions skip changes. One death-check exception has no verified ordinary mission name.
  • Other internal battle and formation conditions can block changes. Their exact tests remain in the technical reference.
  • Manual class changes and transformation items are outside this article.
  • These rules come from US retail code and data. This article adds no new gameplay or visual test.

Class-change glossary

Evolution

An automatic class change. Some happen after battle, some follow an attack, and others happen after a scenario ends.

Stats used for evolution

The game checks the character’s six stats at the end of battle. It does not compare the new class’s starting stats.

Spare equipment

An item you own that nobody has equipped. An item worn by another character is not a spare.

Character identity and class

The game stores identity and class separately for some named characters. Their class can change while their identity stays the same.

Remainder

The amount left after whole-number division. For example, 403 divided by 400 leaves a remainder of 3.

How to read the source and byte evidence

ROM offsets use big-endian z64 order. The master v64 stores each byte pair in reverse order. RAM addresses belong to the stated overlay or structure.

Each code line shows z64 offset, four original bytes, and MIPS assembly. Relative branches name z64 destinations; J/JAL targets are encoded RAM addresses. The next instruction is the branch delay slot.

Samples are stored bytes, not calculated outputs. Decoded resources have separate container and decoded-offset labels. Repository paths identify local sources; this page needs no external files.

Death candidates and Barrier protection

Why can Barrier protection affect an unexpected roster slot?

The builder finds the character's first matching unit and checks its carried Barrier. Its mask uses 32-bit shifts within nominal 64-character banks, so some IDs share bits. Protection is not an independent bit for every character.

Start here: Check membership and carried items, then the exact writer and reader bit operations for the affected roster IDs.

CHARACTER & CAMPAIGN

Scenario Rewards

What the rewards include

Scenario completion can add Goth and Soldiers to your reserves. These two rewards use different calculations.

RewardInputs
GothScenario base Goth, captured stronghold population, and Chaos Frame
Soldier ReservesEach captured stronghold’s population and town Morale, plus room in the reserves

This article covers these population-based rewards. It does not list every scripted item or story reward.

Which strongholds count

Both calculations use the current scenario’s strongholds marked as captured when rewards are calculated. Strongholds without that mark do not contribute.

The game can mark a final stronghold captured before totaling rewards. That stronghold then counts too.

Population is the stronghold’s stored population. Town Morale belongs to that stronghold; Chaos Frame belongs to the army.

Character Alignment is not an input to either reward formula. Capturing strongholds can separately change Chaos Frame before settlement.

Goth formula

First add the population of every counted stronghold. Then calculate the population bonus from Chaos Frame.

If Chaos Frame is below 50:
Population bonus = round down((50 − Chaos Frame) × Total population / 25)
If Chaos Frame is 50 or higher:
Population bonus = round down((Chaos Frame − 50) × Total population / 50)
Goth reward = Base Goth + Population bonus

Round down means discard the fraction. Base Goth is a fixed amount from the scenario’s data.

ScenarioBase Goth
Tenne Plains500
Volmus Mine I600
Volmus Mine II1,500
Alba2,250

At Chaos Frame 50, the population bonus is zero. You still get the base Goth.

If no strongholds count, the population bonus is also zero. The base Goth is separate.

Moving farther from 50 increases the bonus. The low-Chaos-Frame side increases twice as fast as the high side for the same population.

Town Morale does not enter this Goth formula. The reward reads Chaos Frame; it does not change Chaos Frame.

Goth limit

New Goth = min(9,999,999, Current Goth + Goth reward)

You cannot keep more than 9,999,999 Goth through this addition. Any part above that limit is lost.

Goth example

Suppose the scenario’s base reward is 5,000 Goth and counted population totals 1,000. These are example inputs, not a named mission.

Chaos FramePopulation bonusGoth reward
050 × 1,000 / 25 = 2,0007,000
4010 × 1,000 / 25 = 4005,400
5005,000
6010 × 1,000 / 50 = 2005,200
10050 × 1,000 / 50 = 1,0006,000

For a rounding example, Chaos Frame 60 and population 999 give 199.8 bonus Goth. Round down to 199 before adding the base reward.

Soldier Reserve formula

Calculate each counted stronghold separately. Multiply its population by its town Morale, divide by 10,000, and round down.

Soldiers from one stronghold =
max(1, round down(Population × Effective Morale / 10,000))
Stronghold total = sum of the separate stronghold contributions
Calculated Soldiers = remainder after dividing Stronghold total by 256

Each counted stronghold gives at least one Soldier, even if its calculation rounds to zero. No counted strongholds means zero Soldiers.

Effective Morale normally means the town’s Morale. If the town has the special “no Morale” value, use 50 instead.

Chaos Frame and character Alignment do not enter this formula. There is no random roll.

Reserve limit

Room in reserves = 200 − Current Soldier Reserves
Soldiers added = min(Calculated Soldiers, Room in reserves)

Soldier Reserves stop at 200. If only two places remain, a calculated award of five adds only two.

Before the reserve limit, a total of 256 or more wraps: keep the remainder after division by 256. For example, 256 becomes zero.

That wrap matters for unusually large totals or modified data. The technical reference keeps the exact arithmetic and normal-state assumptions.

Soldier example

Counted strongholdPopulationEffective MoraleContribution
A50060500 × 60 / 10,000 = 3
B30040300 × 40 / 10,000 = 1.2 → 1
C5000 → minimum 1

These three strongholds give 3 + 1 + 1 = 5 Soldiers. With reserves at 198, only two are added, bringing reserves to 200.

Rounding happens per stronghold, before adding contributions. Do not combine all populations and use one average Morale.

A counted stronghold with population 200 and the special missing-Morale value uses Morale 50. It contributes one Soldier.

Related rules

Stronghold capture can change Chaos Frame through a separate rule. See Alignment and strongholds.

Angel Knight and Zombie changes happen in later scenario-completion processing. See Automatic Class Changes.

Reward glossary

Population

The population stored for a stronghold. Goth uses the total from counted strongholds; Soldiers use each stronghold separately.

Town Morale

The stronghold’s local Morale value. It affects its Soldier contribution, but this reward formula does not use it for Goth.

Chaos Frame

The army’s hidden reputation value, normally from 0 through 100. It changes the population bonus paid in Goth. It is separate from a character’s Alignment and a town’s Morale.

Base Goth

The fixed Goth amount stored for the scenario. The population bonus is added to it.

Round down

Discard the fractional part of a nonnegative result. For example, 1.8 becomes 1.

Modder reference: Scenario Rewards

Separate reward inputs, calculated awards, and admitted balance changes. Base Goth, captured-site population, and Morale are stored inputs; Chaos Frame affects Goth, while Morale affects Soldiers.

What do you want to change or understand?

How do I change one scenario's base Goth?

Find the staged scenario key in the twelve-byte resource table. Base Goth is one unsigned halfword; the population bonus is calculated separately.

Start with Scenario resource table and base Goth · Scenario settlement, Goth and balance caps

Which towns contribute to the reward?

The helpers scan live site rows whose captured flag is set. The completion path can mark the final site captured before calculating rewards.

Start with Sum captured stronghold population · Stronghold population and Morale resource · Scenario settlement, Goth and balance caps

Why were fewer Soldiers or Goth added than calculated?

Check Soldier byte wrap, then the reserve or wallet cap. Internal key 54 calculates both rewards but skips their transfers.

Start with Per-town Soldier award and byte wrap · Scenario settlement, Goth and balance caps

How to read the source and byte evidence

ROM offsets use big-endian z64 order. The master v64 stores each byte pair in reverse order. RAM addresses belong to the stated overlay or structure.

Each code line shows z64 offset, four original bytes, and MIPS assembly. Relative branches name z64 destinations; J/JAL targets are encoded RAM addresses. The next instruction is the branch delay slot.

Samples are stored bytes, not calculated outputs. Decoded resources have separate container and decoded-offset labels. Repository paths identify local sources; this page needs no external files.

Scenario settlement, Goth and balance caps

Where should I compare calculated rewards with actual payments?

Settlement adds base Goth to a population bonus determined by Chaos Frame's distance from 50. It then caps the wallet and Soldier Reserves. Below 50, the population divisor is 25; otherwise it is 50.

Start here: Compare stored inputs, calculated awards, and admitted balance increases separately. Check the staged key before expecting a transfer.

Stored or calculated?
Computed awards become stored balances; the wallet cap is 9,999,999 and reserve cap is 200.

Sum captured stronghold population

Why does a site's population count or not count?

Only live rows with captured mask 0x0002 contribute. Mask 0x0004 alone does not qualify. The helper sums unsigned population over the current live count, rather than scanning every static stronghold record.

Start here: Check each live site's captured flag and population, then follow the total into Goth settlement.

Per-town Soldier award and byte wrap

Why is summing per-town Soldier awards important?

Each captured town decodes Morale, calculates its contribution, and substitutes one when the rounded result is zero. The helper adds those contributions and returns only the low byte. A sum of 256 therefore returns zero before the reserve cap.

Start here: Decode FF as Morale 50; otherwise mask off the high bit. Follow per-town rounding, low-byte return, then reserve capacity.

Stored or calculated?
Stored population and Morale feed computed contributions and a narrowed award.
Before you edit
Custom populations need the documented single- then double-precision order. The runtime 0.01 coefficient is verified; its cited ROM placement remains supported.
Inspect original source, bytes, and field layout

Decode Morale:FF→50,otherwise raw&7F. Apply single-precision population*(Morale/100), then double*0.01 and truncate. Zero contributes1. Sum returns low byte.

Verified static; canonical semantics accepted

COMBAT SYSTEMS

Status Effects

Effects at a glance

Status effects change what a character can do during battle. Some also change the attributes used by combat calculations.

This page covers character battle conditions and temporary attribute modifiers. Map items, carried unit items, and quest systems have separate rules.

EffectWhat changes
DeathA character with no HP cannot take ordinary actions.
PetrificationThe character cannot act normally, and the condition can survive the battle.
SleepThe character loses actions while asleep.
ParalysisThe character loses actions while paralyzed.
PoisonReduces STR, VIT, INT, MEN, AGI, DEX, and Luck by approximately 10% of their battle baselines.
Power UpAdds approximately 10% of baseline STR, VIT, INT, MEN, AGI, DEX, and Luck per application.
Power DownSubtracts approximately 10% of baseline STR, VIT, INT, MEN, AGI, DEX, and Luck per application.

Death

A character with no HP cannot take ordinary actions.

Existing undead roster members have a separate full-HP restoration at scenario completion. Permanent undead removal is different from ordinary death.

QuestionAnswer
What causes it?Lethal damage. Undead removal has a separate rule below.
How long does it last?Death can remain after combat.
How do I remove it?Altar of Resurrection restores HP, including from zero.

Petrification

The character cannot act normally, and the condition can survive the battle.

Petrification also blocks automatic evolution while it remains active.

QuestionAnswer
What causes it?Gaze of Terror, Petrify; Ji’ylga’s Bow can also inflict it.
How long does it last?Persists after combat until cured.
Can it stack?A second application does not add another layer.
How do I remove it?Revive Stone or Altar of Resurrection. Combined Healing and combined Healing Plus also remove Petrification during battle.
Who is immune?Hallowed Shield and Celestial Veil protect against it. Class examples include Soldier, Ghost, Cockatrice, Stone Golem, Baldr Golem, Gladiator, Vanguard, General. Some named enemies have additional immunities.

Training and some event battles restore saved HP and status instead of keeping a new Petrification result.

This condition can exclude a character from combined spells and grouped Soldier attacks.

Gaze of Terror fails against a target carrying a Light Shield or Heavy Shield. Without a shield, it bypasses the ordinary accuracy roll.

Petrification immunity still blocks Gaze of Terror. Other Petrification sources use their own success rules.

Sleep

The character loses actions while asleep.

Nominal recovery chance per affected action is min(Luck + 1, 100)%. Equipment Luck is not added separately.

For Luck 50, 51 of the 100 possible roll results recover: a nominal 51% chance.

The recovery action is still spent. A successful, nonlethal physical hit also gives a wake-up check unless the target is paralyzed or petrified. A sleep weapon can reapply Sleep after the check.

QuestionAnswer
What causes it?Mesmerize, Abyss, Clear Disaster, Evil Dead, Slumber Mist, Nightmare, Ionosphere, Atmosphere, Deep Sleep, Infest, Inferno, Black Breeze; Evil Blade and Brionac.
How long does it last?Until recovery, a status cure, or the end of combat.
Can it stack?Repeating this effect does not add another layer. Direct spells, extra effects, and weapon hits combine or replace ailments differently.
How do I remove it?Recovery checks, combined Healing, or combined Healing Plus.
Who is immune?Hallowed Shield, Purified Robe, and Freude Helm protect against it. Class examples include Lich, Vampire, Zombie, Skeleton, Ghost, Golem, Stone Golem, Baldr Golem. Some named enemies have additional immunities.

This condition can exclude a character from combined spells and grouped Soldier attacks.

Paralysis

The character loses actions while paralyzed.

At each affected action, the recovery roll uses the same Luck comparison as Sleep. Recovering still spends that action.

If Sleep and Paralysis coexist, the action dispatcher processes Paralysis first.

Luck 50 gives a nominal 51% recovery chance per affected action. Equipment Luck is not added separately.

QuestionAnswer
What causes it?Radiant Gale, Shock Bolt, Ray of Paralysis, Plasma Ball, Plasma Storm, Bind Flare, Lava Shot, Lava Flow, Poison Plant; Dagda’s Hammer and Doll of Curse.
How long does it last?Until recovery, a status cure, or the end of combat.
Can it stack?Repeating this effect does not add another layer. Direct spells, extra effects, and weapon hits combine or replace ailments differently.
How do I remove it?Recovery checks, combined Healing, or combined Healing Plus.
Who is immune?Hallowed Shield, Saint’s Shield, and Elder’s Sign protect against it. Class examples include Lich, Vampire, Zombie, Skeleton, Ghost, Golem, Stone Golem, Baldr Golem. Some named enemies have additional immunities.

Poison Plant inflicts Paralysis despite its name.

This condition can exclude a character from combined spells and grouped Soldier attacks.

Poison

Reduces STR, VIT, INT, MEN, AGI, DEX, and Luck by approximately 10% of their battle baselines.

HP, maximum HP, and level are not reduced by this attribute calculation.

Poison does not replace an ordinary action with a recovery action. Its verified penalty is to attributes.

QuestionAnswer
What causes it?Poison Cloud, Clay Assault, Blue Spiral, Poison Lime, Doom
How long does it last?Until a status cure or the end of combat.
Can it stack?Repeated Poison does not add another penalty. Whether other ailments coexist depends on the attack path.
How do I remove it?Combined Healing and combined Healing Plus remove Poison.
Who is immune?Hallowed Shield protects against it. Class examples include Lich, Vampire, Zombie, Skeleton, Ghost, Gorgon, Golem, Stone Golem, Baldr Golem. Some named enemies have additional immunities.

Direct status spells can preserve other ailments. Extra effects and weapon hits use different replacement rules.

A weapon can replace Poison without immediately restoring the reduced attributes. Do not assume that replacement instantly restores the reduced values.

Power Up

Adds approximately 10% of baseline STR, VIT, INT, MEN, AGI, DEX, and Luck per application.

It changes battle attributes without adding levels or maximum HP.

QuestionAnswer
What causes it?The friendly Throw a Kiss variant.
How long does it last?Temporary battle modifier; not saved as permanent attribute growth.
Can it stack?Repeated applications add baseline-sized steps. Power Down subtracts from the same modifier.
How do I remove it?Power Down offsets it. Combined Healing and combined Healing Plus do not erase the Power modifier.
Who is immune?The usual ailment-protecting equipment and class immunities do not block this modifier.

Power Down

Subtracts approximately 10% of baseline STR, VIT, INT, MEN, AGI, DEX, and Luck per application.

Its first application has the same ordinary attribute result as Poison. Both together subtract approximately 20% of baseline.

QuestionAnswer
What causes it?Throw a Kiss, Crimson Note, Earthquake, Dark Blaze, Dark Flame; Throw a Kiss uses its hostile variant.
How long does it last?Temporary battle modifier; not saved as permanent attribute loss.
Can it stack?Repeated applications add penalties. Power Up offsets them. Poison adds another baseline-sized penalty.
How do I remove it?Power Up offsets it. Combined Healing and combined Healing Plus do not erase the Power modifier.
Who is immune?The usual ailment-protecting equipment and class immunities do not block this modifier.

Power and Poison together

Start with the character’s saved attributes before temporary battle modifiers. Each recalculation reads those values; it does not multiply already modified battle attributes again.

Power Up adds a tenth of baseline per application. Power Down subtracts a tenth. Poison subtracts one additional tenth.

This can affect damage, defense, accuracy, evasion, and Luck checks. A 10% attribute change does not guarantee a 10% final damage change.

Approximate attribute = Baseline × (1 + 0.1 × Power Up count − 0.1 × Power Down count − Poison penalty)
Poison penalty = 0.1 while poisoned; otherwise 0
ExampleResult
Baseline attribute: 200200
Poison alone180
One Power Down180
Poison and one Power Down160
One Power Up220
Two Power Up applications240
Poison and one Power Up200

The game uses floating-point arithmetic, then discards the fractional part. The simple percentage formula can differ at rounding boundaries.

Ordinary attributes are limited to 0–999 after conversion. Luck is limited to 0–100.

These changes do not grant temporary levels. Automatic class changes can nevertheless read temporary attributes; their exact timing matters.

Temporary attributes and evolution

Power Up changes attributes, not levels. An automatic evolution can use those temporary attributes when it checks its stat requirements.

For example, one Young Dragon row needs VIT 114, INT 73, and MEN 101. Baselines of 110, 70, and 95 fail.

One Power Up gives 121, 77, and 104, which meet those three requirements. Other class-change requirements still apply.

An actual level-up happens before the evolution check. That path reloads persistent attributes and overwrites the earlier temporary values.

This is a conditional result from the original code. It is not a guarantee that every battle exit triggers evolution.

Cures and undead removal

OperationWhat the evidence establishes
Ailment cureCombined Healing and combined Healing Plus clear Petrification, Sleep, Paralysis, and Poison after success. They do not erase Power changes.
Ordinary HealingIndividual Healing and Healing Plus restore HP without the combined versions’ ailment cure. Ordinary healing does not revive a dead character.
Undead removalBanish, Jihad, Magic Missile, Sacred Breath, Divine Ray, and Ignis Fatuus can remove eligible undead after a successful lethal amount.
Eligible undeadEligible targets are Zombies, Skeletons, and Ghosts. An attack name or Virtue element alone does not establish removal.
Removal after lethal damageNormal combat removes the character from the roster and unit. Altar of Resurrection cannot bring back that removed character.
Training and special event battlesTraining skips permanent removal. A separate event-battle preservation exception also exists.
Removal weaponsBlessed Sword, Penitence, Oracion, Chaladholg, Kusanagi, Needle of Light, Anbicion, Clau Solace, Celestial Hammer, Rune Axe, Holy Lance, Lance of Longinus, Holy Comet, Vajra, Crescente, Ytival, Celestial Mace, Gambantein, Airgetlam, Heaven's Doll, Lia Fail, Caldia. Their removal flag still requires the eligible lethal-undead path.

Attacks and equipment

Some attacks inflict an ailment directly. Others must hit first and then pass another accuracy-based check.

The table lists distinct attack names from all 158 action records. Repeated names can represent different target areas or effect variants.

Direct status attacks normally use their accuracy threshold, then immunity. Gaze of Terror has the shield exception described above. Extra effects can require another roll below half or one quarter of that threshold.

A successful nonlethal physical weapon hit can apply its ailment without an extra status roll. Immunity and special transformation branches still matter.

An immunity or existing-state rejection can still prevent an extra effect after its listed success condition passes.

AttacksEffect and success condition
Mesmerize, Abyss, Clear Disaster, Evil Dead, Atmosphere, InfernoSleep — hit first, then roll below half the accuracy threshold
Throw a KissPower Up — no extra success roll; eligibility still applies
Throw a Kiss, EarthquakePower Down — primary action must succeed
Gaze of TerrorPetrification — fails against a Light or Heavy Shield; otherwise passes the ordinary success gate, then checks immunity
Banish, Jihad, Magic Missile, Sacred Breath, Divine Ray, Ignis FatuusUndead removal — successful lethal amount against eligible undead
PetrifyPetrification — hit first, then roll below half the accuracy threshold
Radiant Gale, Plasma Storm, Lava FlowParalysis — hit first, then roll below half the accuracy threshold
Crimson Note, Dark FlamePower Down — hit first, then roll below half the accuracy threshold
Shock Bolt, Ray of Paralysis, Bind Flare, Poison PlantParalysis — direct effect: pass accuracy and immunity
Poison Cloud, Poison Lime, DoomPoison — direct effect: pass accuracy and immunity
Slumber Mist, Nightmare, Deep Sleep, Black BreezeSleep — direct effect: pass accuracy and immunity
Combined Healing, combined Healing PlusStatus cure — primary action must succeed
Ionosphere, InfestSleep — hit first, then roll below one quarter of the accuracy threshold
Plasma Ball, Lava ShotParalysis — hit first, then roll below one quarter of the accuracy threshold
Clay AssaultPoison — hit first, then roll below one quarter of the accuracy threshold
Blue SpiralPoison — hit first, then roll below half the accuracy threshold
Dark BlazePower Down — hit first, then roll below one quarter of the accuracy threshold

What this guide establishes

The finite inventory covers seven character conditions or modifiers, plus the related cure and undead-removal operations.

Status names do not predict behavior. Poison Plant applies Paralysis; Doom applies Poison.

Immunity can come from either class identity. Special enemy versions of a class can have different protection.

The technical reference lists exact branches, rounding, source records, and research limits.

No fixed number of seconds was established. Fatigue, permanent stat items, class changes, and scenario squad effects are separate systems.

Carried unit items can affect separate campaign and combat command systems. This page covers character battle conditions and temporary attribute modifiers.

Related rules: Combined-spell recipes · Accuracy and evasion · Automatic class changes · Fatigue.

Status glossary

Battle baseline

The character’s saved attributes before temporary battle modifiers. Each rebuild reads those saved values; equipment bonuses remain separate.

Recovery check

A chance to remove Sleep or Paralysis when the character reaches an action. Recovering still uses that action.

Power step

One Power Up or Power Down changes the battle modifier by about one tenth of the baseline attributes.

Modder reference: Status Effects

Start with the behavior you want to investigate. Attack descriptors, actor flags, temporary arithmetic, and persistent character data have different roles.

What do you want to change or understand?

Change which status an attack inflicts?

Locate its action record, then follow the primary or secondary condition and immunity filter.

Start with Trace a named attack to its status rule · Check the right immunity category · Apply, combine, or cure effects · Gaze of Terror shield override

Change Power or Poison strength?

Follow the shared baseline rebuild. Check stacking, conversion, limits, and export before treating a changed coefficient as a complete modification.

Start with Rebuild temporary attributes · Separate battle attributes from persistent growth

Change recovery or cure behavior?

Recovery spends an action. Ailment cures and battle export clear different state, so start with the exact lifecycle.

Start with Sleep recovery action · Apply, combine, or cure effects · Separate battle attributes from persistent growth

Investigate evolution or permanent removal?

Both depend on result ordering and persistent state. A temporary status flag alone does not explain the outcome.

Start with Follow temporary stats into evolution · Separate lethal undead removal from death

How to read the source and byte evidence

ROM offsets use big-endian z64 order. The master v64 stores each byte pair in reverse order. RAM addresses belong to the stated overlay or structure.

Each code line shows z64 offset, four original bytes, and MIPS assembly. Relative branches name z64 destinations; J/JAL targets are encoded RAM addresses. The next instruction is the branch delay slot.

Samples are stored bytes, not calculated outputs. Decoded resources have separate container and decoded-offset labels. Repository paths identify local sources; this page needs no external files.

Apply, combine, or cure effects

Why do spells, extra effects, and weapons combine ailments differently?

This secondary-effect dispatcher tests existing flags. Direct status spells set flags without these exclusions. Weapon hits replace lower-priority ailments. Cure clears ailment flags without resetting Power.

Start here: Follow func_0022B06C after the attack or equipment path has passed its success and immunity checks.

Stored or calculated?
Battle actor +0x40 stores flags. Effect codes in attack results select behavior; they are not flag masks.

Changing a mask changes application order interactions. Byte identity does not validate a new rule.

Rebuild temporary attributes

Does Power change levels or multiply the last displayed stat?

Power changes accumulate as floating-point steps. The rebuild reads baseline attributes and adds baseline times the effective modifier. Poison subtracts one tenth from that modifier. HP and level are outside this calculation.

Start here: Start with func_0021D450, then its Power Up, Power Down, and rebuild-only wrappers.

Stored or calculated?
The accumulator is stored battle state. The seven resulting attributes are calculated values; they are not seven independent ROM constants.
Before you edit
A changed coefficient needs arithmetic, conversion, bound, export, and evolution checks. This entry is an investigation start, not a tested patch.

Separate battle attributes from persistent growth

Why do battle modifiers disappear instead of becoming permanent growth?

The export path clears Sleep, Paralysis, and Poison, resets the Power accumulator, and rebuilds baseline attributes before persistent writes. Battle snapshot restoration is a separate part of this function.

Start here: Compare func_0021C140 with the level-up caller func_00219470 and actor reload func_0021C074.

Stored or calculated?
Persistent character attributes and battle attributes are distinct representations. Export calculates clean values before storing them.
Before you edit
Changing export can affect saves and class changes. No save-writing patch is established here.

Sleep recovery action

Does waking up give the character its action back?

Recovery compares a random remainder against current raw Luck. A successful recovery clears Sleep but still consumes the affected action. Paralysis uses a parallel action path.

Start here: Read func_0022EDD4 for Sleep and func_0022EC08 for Paralysis; physical wake-up is in func_0022A964.

Stored or calculated?
Luck is a calculated battle attribute. The recovery comparison is code, not a duration counter.
Before you edit
An altered threshold must retain action consumption and distinguish physical-hit waking from ordinary recovery.

Check the right immunity category

Which class or equipment flag blocks a specific ailment?

The status-specific filter maps effect IDs to immunity categories. The actor immunity builder combines class and equipment evidence. Power Up and Power Down do not use those four ailment categories.

Start here: Start with func_002379AC, then func_0021062C and the class/equipment census in the lifecycle evidence.

Stored or calculated?
Class and equipment flags are stored parameters. The actor immunity result combines them; class names alone are insufficient.

Trace a named attack to its status rule

Where do I start to change which status an attack applies?

An action record selects a primary effect and an optional secondary effect. Secondary conditions decide whether an extra accuracy check or lethal result is required.

Start here: Use action ID and D0 indexing from the source census. Compare the descriptor with func_0022D14C before changing an effect.

Stored or calculated?
These samples are stored action bytes. D0 is the data origin, four bytes after the name pointer; its twelve bytes exclude the next name pointer.
Before you edit
Changing the effect byte alone can leave incompatible target, animation, or condition behavior. This evidence establishes decoding, not safe patch combinations.

Follow temporary stats into evolution

Can a Power boost meet an evolution requirement early?

Actual level-up exports, permanently grows, and reloads attributes before evolution. Without that reload, the evolution selector can read temporary battle stats.

Start here: Compare the level-up branch in func_00219470 with the current-stat checks in func_00219730 and reload func_0021C074.

Stored or calculated?
Evolution thresholds are stored data; current battle stats are calculated values. Neither is a temporary level.
Before you edit
Changing timing changes which representation evolution sees. Preserve every other evolution gate and test both level-up and no-level-up paths.

Separate lethal undead removal from death

Why can a defeated undead character disappear instead of waiting for revival?

The removal event follows a lethal result against eligible undead. Normal combat clears roster identity and membership; Training and the event preservation condition bypass removal.

Start here: Follow effect 7 through the recorded event 0x31 to func_0021EBBC, then persistent removal func_0004196C.

Stored or calculated?
The effect marker schedules an event. The event changes roster identity and unit membership; it is not a persistent ailment byte.
Before you edit
Do not turn a lethal-result condition into an unconditional kill. Review Training, event preservation, side, roster identity, and membership before editing.
Inspect original source, bytes, and field layout

Gaze of Terror shield override

Why does Gaze of Terror ignore the usual accuracy result?

Its D5=3 override replaces that result with a shield check. Any Light or Heavy Shield among four equipment slots makes the action fail; ordinary immunity follows.

Start here: Follow func_0022D14C into shield predicate func_0020C3B4 and item-type getter func_000454c8.

Stored or calculated?
D5 and item types are stored selectors. Primary success is a calculated boolean that this branch replaces.
Before you edit
Changing this selector can replace a whole success rule. Keep target eligibility and Petrification immunity distinct from the shield test.
Inspect original source, bytes, and field layout

D5=3 replaces the ordinary accuracy outcome with the absence of a Light or Heavy Shield. The primary Petrification immunity check still follows.

Verified static bytes and source-derived semantics; independently accepted within the stated scope in review R2.
